The Nine Cafe celebrates Mediterranean flavours with an eco-conscious twist, pairing Five Senses espresso with seasonal organic ingredients. Rich flat whites and aromatic long blacks complement dishes like shakshuka-inspired bowls. Bright interiors, lush greenery and soft lighting create a serene coffee environment. Committed to sustainability, The Nine uses compostable packaging and ethically sourced beans, making it a top choice for environmentally minded coffee lovers seeking quality brews in Bondi Beach.
9. Gertrude & Alice Bookstore Cafe

Gertrude & Alice Bookstore Cafe is Bondi Beach’s literary oasis, blending rare books with specialty coffee. Baristas craft expertly balanced espressos, creamy cappuccinos and smooth filter brews from premium beans. Guests browse vintage paperbacks or lounge in cozy nooks while sipping seasonal single-origin coffees that highlight bright acidity and rich sweetness. With timber bookshelves, soft jazz and an intimate atmosphere, Gertrude & Alice offers a unique coffee experience that nourishes both mind and palate.
10. The Crabbe Hole Cafe

Perched beside the iconic Bondi Icebergs pool, The Crabbe Hole Cafe delivers a quintessential Bondi Beach coffee experience. This unpretentious spot doubles down on quality, serving double-shot espressos, bold long blacks and silky flat whites alongside a concise menu of toasted sandwiches and treats. Floor-to-ceiling windows frame sweeping ocean vistas, inviting patrons to sip hearty coffees before or after a swim. With minimalist décor and salt-tinged sea air, The Crabbe Hole is a local caffeine sanctuary.
11. Blackwood Bondi

Blackwood Bondi (Shop 3/87–89 Glenayr Ave) is an upmarket Bondi Beach café from the team behind Blackwood Cronulla, blending Michelin-trained finesse and bold coffee creations. Baristas craft coconut lychee matcha lattes, signature biscoff lattes and robust espressos from specialty beans. Paired with dishes like truffled chilli scrambled eggs and blueberry ricotta hotcakes, the café’s refined interior and coastal-chic vibe make it a must-stop for coffee aficionados seeking innovative brews by the sea.

blocks.text: Don’t let a rainy day in Bondi Beach dampen your spirits. Discover 7 fantastic indoor activities-from art and dining to wellness and shopping-to keep you entertained and dry.

Bondi Beach is world-renowned for its sun, surf and sand-but even here, rain can put a pause on beach plans. Fortunately, this vibrant suburb boasts a thriving indoor scene that’ll keep you busy until the skies clear. Whether you’re craving culture, comfort food, retail therapy or a wellness reset, Bondi Beach has you covered. Read on to uncover seven top indoor experiences that turn a soggy day into an unexpectedly delightful adventure.
1. Bondi Pavilion: Art Exhibitions & Live Performances

Nestled at the southern end of the beach, the heritage-listed Bondi Pavilion is your go-to cultural hotspot when it’s pouring outside. Wander through rotating art exhibitions showcasing local talent, catch a live theatre or comedy show in the intimate auditorium, or sign up for a weekend workshop-from mosaic-making to improv. Regular events include film nights, poetry readings and community markets under cover. With its historic charm and circular calendar of creative happenings, the Pavilion ensures that rainy days in Bondi Beach feel anything but gloomy.
2. Icebergs Dining Room & Bar: Iconic Indoor Dining with Ocean Views

Perched above the famous Icebergs Pool, Icebergs Dining Room & Bar offers panoramic coastal vistas without a drop of water on your jacket. The sleek interior, designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, invites you to watch stormy seas roll in while indulging in modern Australian cuisine. Share a plate of truffle-scented arancini, pair fresh ocean trout with a crisp glass of Chardonnay, or simply cozy up at the bar with barista-style coffee or a signature cocktail. It’s the perfect refuge for gastronomes and sea-lovers alike on a wet Bondi Beach afternoon.
3. Cozy Cafés: Bondi’s Best Rain-Safe Coffee Spots

When clouds gather, Bondi’s café scene shines brighter than ever. Duck into Porch & Parlour for cloud-like sourdough pancakes, savour the single-origin brews and artisanal pastries at Speedos Café, or unwind with a matcha latte in the Scandinavian-inspired Sedici. Many cafés offer board games, free Wi-Fi and nook-style seating, making them ideal work-from-café hideouts. Pro tip: ask for a window seat-you’ll get people-watching vibes and the soothing soundtrack of raindrops tapping on glass.
4. Wellness Retreats: Spa Treatments & Yoga Studios

Rainy days are tailor-made for self-care. Treat yourself to a hydrating facial or deep-tissue massage at Endota Spa Bondi-their heated treatment rooms and eucalyptus steam rooms will melt stress away. If you prefer movement, Yoga Bogan and Bondi Life Centre both offer drop-in classes ranging from hot yoga to restorative yin. Guided meditation sessions and sound-bath workshops are also on the calendar. Afterward, you’ll feel rejuvenated, rehydrated and ready to tackle any puddle that dares to cross your path.
5. Westfield Bondi Junction Cinemas: Latest Releases & Indie Flicks

Just a short bus ride from the beachfront, Westfield Bondi Junction houses a multi-screen cinema complex showcasing everything from Hollywood blockbusters to arthouse gems. Treat yourself to a matinee (often cheaper on weekdays), complete with reclining seats and gourmet snacks. Many sessions run daily, so you can easily fit a film into any storm window. Bonus: the adjoining food court and restaurants mean post-movie brunch or dinner is just a few steps away.
6. Westfield Bondi Junction Shopping: Retail Therapy Under Cover

Make a beeline for Westfield Bondi Junction’s sprawling indoor mall when you need to stay bone-dry. Over 300 stores span fashion, beauty, electronics and homewares-browse local labels at Spell, score a bargain at UNIQLO, or pick up surf gear at Rip Curl. Don’t miss the international food hall for quick bites, or venture to LEVEL K for boutique designers. With undercover parking, public transport links and seamless internal walkways, it’s the ultimate retail refuge on a gloomy Bondi Beach day.
7. Bondi Wholefoods: Hands-On Cooking Classes

For a truly immersive indoor experience, roll up your sleeves at Bondi Wholefoods’s cooking studio. Their weekend classes teach everything from vegan baking and plant-based brunch to homemade pasta or sushi-rolling. Guided by expert chefs, you’ll learn practical tips, try new flavour combinations and enjoy delicious results you made yourself. Classes run for two to three hours and include all ingredients-plus recipes to recreate your creations at home. It’s a tasty way to turn rainy doldrums into satisfying foodie memories.

Don’t let a bit of rain keep you from exploring all that Bondi Beach has to offer. From cultural havens and world-class dining to retail escapes and hands-on workshops, these indoor activities ensure your rainy-day itinerary is as sunny as the beach itself. Bookmark this guide, pack an umbrella, and get ready to see Bondi Beach in a whole new (indoor) light-rain or shine.

title: 10 Things to Know Before Running the City2Surf
metaDescription: Essential tips to prepare for Sydney’s iconic 14 km City2Surf run-training, strategy, gear, and more.
h1: 10 Things You Need to Know Before Running the City2Surf
intro: 10 Things You Need to Know Before Running the City2Surf — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach 10 Things You Need to Know Before Running the City2Surf The City2Surf is one of Australia’s most celebrated road races, drawing over 80,000 runners each year for its vibrant atmosphere, scenic course from Sydney CBD to

blocks.text: The City2Surf is one of Australia’s most celebrated road races, drawing over 80,000 runners each year for its vibrant atmosphere, scenic course from Sydney CBD to Bondi Beach, and notorious “Heartbreak Hill.” Whether you’re a first-timer or a seasoned runner aiming for a personal best, thorough preparation is key. This guide covers the top 10 things you need to know before lining up at Hyde Park, ensuring you cross the finish line strong, injury-free, and smiling.
1. Know the Course: 14 km with Heartbreak Hill

The City2Surf spans 14 km (8.7 miles), starting at Hyde Park and finishing at Bondi Beach’s foreshore. The first 5 km are relatively flat, but at around the 6 km mark you’ll face “Heartbreak Hill,” a 2 km incline peaking at about 64 m elevation. Training on hills and understanding the course profile helps you conserve energy early and tackle the steep section without burning out. Download the official route map from the City2Surf website to familiarise yourself with water stations, split points, and spectator zones.
2. Secure Your Spot and Start Wave Early

Entries for City2Surf sell out fast-often within weeks of opening in March. Register as soon as entries open to guarantee your bib and preferred start wave. Waves are colour-coded by estimated finish time; choose one that matches your ability (e.g., blue waves for sub-60 min runners, green for 60–75 min). Being in the correct wave not only ensures a smoother flow but also a more accurate chip time and less weaving through slower runners.
3. Train Specifically for Heartbreak Hill

Heartbreak Hill can make or break your race. Incorporate hill repeats into your training at least once a week, focusing on both uphill strength and downhill recovery technique. Aim for 6–8 repeats on a gradient similar to the course (around 5–7%). This builds muscular endurance in quads and glutes, and familiarises your cardiovascular system with sustained effort on an incline. After hill workouts, include easy recovery runs to prevent overuse injuries.
4. Follow a Progressive Training Plan

Your weekly mileage should increase by no more than 10% to avoid injury. Aim for a mix of long runs (up to 16 km), tempo runs, interval sessions, and easy recovery jogs. Schedule rest days or cross-training (cycling, swimming) to allow muscles to repair. If you’re a beginner, a 12-week plan is ideal; more experienced runners may prefer an 8-week tune-up. Consistency-rather than occasional long runs-is the key to building the endurance required for 14 km.
5. Dial In Hydration and Nutrition

Hydration begins days before race day… not just on the morning itself. Aim for 2–3 L of fluids daily in the lead-up, and practise taking on 150–200 mL of water or electrolyte drink every 5 km during training. On race morning, have a light meal 2–3 hours before the start: think toast with nut butter, banana, or a small bowl of oatmeal. Avoid trying new gels or sports drinks on race day-stick to products you’ve tested in training to prevent stomach upsets.
6. Gear Up: Shoes, Apparel, and Sunscreen

Choose well-broken-in running shoes with adequate cushioning for the varied surfaces and hills. Lightweight, moisture-wicking apparel and a cap or visor will keep you comfortable in Sydney’s often warm, sunny conditions. Slip-on arm sleeves can be peeled off mid-race if you overheat. Critically, apply a high-SPF, sweat-resistant sunscreen 20 minutes before the gun-it’s easy to forget until you feel the sting of the midday sun as you approach Bondi.
7. Plan Your Transport to Hyde Park

Race day road closures and crowds can make getting to the start challenging. The closest train stations (St James, Museum) often reach capacity early. Consider buses, ferries to Circular Quay plus a short run, or even ride-sharing to a nearby drop-off. Allow at least 60 minutes extra travel time on race morning to find a gear-check tent, hit the loo, and warm up with dynamic stretches before your wave starts.
8. Check the Weather and Adjust Accordingly

Early August in Sydney can vary from cool and cloudy to unexpectedly warm. In the days before the race, monitor the Bureau of Meteorology forecast and adjust your gear: long sleeves or arm warmers if it’s below 15 °C, or lighter singlets if it’s above 20 °C. On race morning, layer clothing you can shed-trash bags over your gear for warmth on the start line-and leave them at the gear-check or roadside volunteers.
9. Race-Day Pacing and Strategy

Start conservatively: adrenaline and crowds can tempt you to surge early. Stick to your target pace for the first 5 km, then maintain effort up Heartbreak Hill-even if your pace drops slightly, focus on effort rather than splits. Use downhill sections as recovery, but avoid overstriding to prevent quads soreness. If aiming for a time goal, break the race into segments (0–5 km, 5–9 km, 9–14 km), and adjust pace at each checkpoint based on how you feel.
10. Recovery and Post-Race Logistics

After crossing the finish on Bondi’s foreshore, don’t stop abruptly-walk for 5–10 minutes to aid muscle cooling and reduce stiffness. Grab a water and snack from the post-race zone, and use the free ice baths or cool showers if available. Plan your meeting point with friends or family beforehand-mobile service can be patchy in crowds. Finally, treat yourself to brunch or a dip in Bondi Icebergs pool; celebrating properly helps both mind and body recover for your next run.

Successfully running the City2Surf is as much about smart preparation as it is about race-day grit. By understanding the course, training specifically, nailing your nutrition and gear, and planning every detail from transport to pacing, you’ll be primed to tackle those 14 km with confidence. Lace up, follow these tips, and get ready to soak up the energy of Sydney’s biggest running event-and enjoy that well-earned finish-line view of Bondi Beach!

title: Bondi Icebergs FAQ: 20 Questions Answered

h1: Bondi Icebergs Ocean Pool FAQ: 20 Essential Questions Answered (Hours, Fees, Membership & More)
intro: Bondi Icebergs Ocean Pool FAQ: 20 Essential Questions Answered (Hours, Fees, Membership & More) — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Icebergs Ocean Pool FAQ: 20 Essential Questions Answered (Hours, Fees, Membership & More) Bondi Icebergs Ocean Pool is one of the world’s most photographed rock-edge po

blocks.text: Bondi Icebergs Ocean Pool is one of the world’s most photographed rock-edge pools, beloved by locals and visitors alike. Below you’ll find concise answers to the questions we get asked most about visiting, swimming, and joining the Club-everything from opening hours and entry fees to pool dimensions and membership perks.

What are the opening hours? The pool is open Monday–Friday from 6:00 AM to 6:30 PM, and Saturday–Sunday from 6:30 AM to 6:30 PM. It closes every Thursday for cleaning (summer exceptions apply when tides permit).
How much does it cost to swim? Single-visit passes are $10 for adults, $7 for children, and $30 for families. Six-visit and 25-visit multi-passes offer discounts across each category.
Can I buy multi-visit passes in advance? Yes-six-visit and 25-visit passes are available at reception and online at the Club’s website for adults, children, and families.

Are there annual membership options? Social membership (club access only) costs $60 AUD/year. For unlimited pool access plus club benefits, a Social + Pool membership is $650 AUD/year-both valid for 12 months.
Do I need to book a lane? No lane reservations are required for regular swimming-just turn up and swim. However, on special event days (e.g., City2Surf weekend) bookings are essential.
Is towel and locker hire available? Yes-towel hire and locker usage are each available for $5 per item.
Is the pool heated? No-the Bondi Icebergs Pool is fed directly by ocean tides, so water temperature varies with the sea.
Are qualified lifeguards on duty? Yes-both the main lap pool and the kids’ pool are patrolled by qualified lifeguards during all opening hours.
Where is Bondi Icebergs Pool located? You’ll find the pool at 1 Notts Avenue, Bondi Beach NSW 2026-right at the southern end of Bondi’s golden sands.
Is there a dedicated kids’ pool? Yes-a smaller, shallow pool sits adjacent to the main 50 m pool, perfect for young swimmers.
What are the pool dimensions? The main lap pool is 50 m long with nine lanes; the adjacent kids’ pool is 25 m with six lanes, holding roughly 500,000 gallons of seawater.
How often is the pool cleaned? It closes every Thursday for scheduled cleaning and maintenance.
What other facilities are on site? Icebergs offers a café (opens 7:00 AM), gym & sauna (opens 6:00 AM), massage rooms (from 9:00 AM), plus a bistro and licensed bar.
Is sauna access included? Yes-the sauna is included in your pool admission. Maximum 15 minutes per session; please bring your own towel.
When is winter swim season? The Bondi Icebergs Winter Swimming Club swims every Sunday from May through September.

How do I join the swim club? Prospective members must attend a 1.5 hr induction (with a swim time trial), be proposed by current members, and complete qualifying swims. Inductions are held each April.
What’s the history of Bondi Icebergs? Founded in 1929 by local lifesavers, Icebergs became licensed in 1960, admitted female members in 1995, and opened its current premises in 2002.
Do public holidays affect opening hours? Yes-trading hours may vary on public holidays. Always check the Club’s website or call ahead.
Is there a live pool camera? A live-streaming pool camera is being upgraded to fibre internet for a smoother HD feed-check the Club’s site for updates.
How can I contact Bondi Icebergs? For pool enquiries call (02) 9130 4804; for Club matters call (02) 9130 3120; or email reception@icebergs.com.au

blocks.text: Bondi Beach is one of Sydney’s most iconic coastal neighbourhoods, where golden sands meet a buzzing café and restaurant scene from dawn’s first coffee to dusk’s beachfront cocktails. Locals and visitors alike flock here for early-morning swims in the rock pools, surf lessons, designer boutiques-and nights spent at vibrant bars overlooking the Pacific Ocean.
How to Get to Bondi Beach
Bondi is just 13 km (8 mi) east of Sydney Airport (SYD), which handles domestic and international flights daily. From the terminals you can:
Hire a car, taxi or rideshare service
Catch the SkyBus shuttle into the city, then transfer to a train or bus to Bondi Junction
Take a train from Central Station to Bondi Junction, then hop on one of the frequent buses that drop you right at the beach .
Parking is scarce at Bondi itself, so public transport or rideshares are highly recommended for stress-free arrival.
Best Time to Visit Bondi Beach
Summer (December–February): Warm, sunny days make for perfect beach lounging and ocean-pool swims.

Spring (September–November): Sunny, milder temperatures and lower humidity-ideal for coastal walks. Don’t miss the Sculpture by the Sea exhibition along the Bondi to Tamarama walk in October and November .
Autumn (March–May): Shoulder-season comfort with fewer crowds.
Winter (June–August): Cooler, but keep an eye out for migrating whales from late June to mid-July along the headland .
Top Things to Do in Bondi Beach
1. Take the Bondi to Tamarama Coastal Walk & Sculpture by the Sea

Stroll the 2 km cliffside track from Bondi to Tamarama Beach to soak up panoramic ocean views and encounter the annual Sculpture by the Sea outdoor gallery (Oct–Nov). It’s a feast for the eyes and camera-and only a short train-and-bus ride from the city.
2. Swim at the Iconic Bondi Icebergs Ocean Pool

Carved into the cliff at Bondi’s southern end, the Bondi Icebergs pool dates back to 1929 and offers invigorating sea-spray swims with unmatched coastal vistas. Open year-round, it’s perfect for a chilly winter dip or sunrise workout-just bring your towel and entry fee (around AUD 9).
3. Learn to Surf with a Lesson at Bondi Beach

Bondi’s consistent, beginner-friendly waves make it one of Australia’s top surf schools. Certified instructors provide boards, wetsuits, and safety guidance, so you can stand up on your first wave with confidence. Morning sessions are best for calmer water and fewer crowds.
4. Stroll Through the Vibrant Bondi Markets

Held every weekend at Bondi Beach Public School, the Bondi Markets showcase local designers, vintage finds, handcrafted jewellery, fresh produce and street food. Arrive early for the best picks-and enjoy live music in true beach-vibe style.
5. Relax on the Golden Sands

Whether you’re sunbathing, people-watching or reading under an umbrella, Bondi’s wide, golden shoreline is made for leisurely beach days. Lifeguards patrol flagged swimming zones, so you can relax knowing you’re in safe hands.
6. Indulge in Café Culture & Beachside Bars

From pre-dawn flat whites to sunset cocktails, Bondi’s café and bar scene is top-notch. Grab a smashed avocado toast at a Campbell Parade café, then return later for craft beers or cocktails at one of the beachfront bars-perfect for people-watching as the sky turns pink.
7. Visit the Historic Bondi Pavilion

Built in 1929, the Bondi Pavilion is a cultural hub housing galleries, theatres, studios and a casual café. Check the events calendar for art exhibitions, live music and workshops-plus it’s a great spot for coffee with a view over the sand.
8. Spot Whales from Bondi Headland

In winter, head to the cliffs for some of Sydney’s best whale-watching. Humpbacks migrate north along the coastline from late June to mid-July, offering breathtaking encounters with breaching whales against a dramatic seascape.

blocks.text: Bondi is world-famous for its sun, surf and sand, but rainy days here can be just as memorable. Whether you’re seeking culture, adventure or pure relaxation, this guide shows you how to make the most of Bondi-rain or shine.
1. Explore the Bondi Pavilion Cultural Hub

The Bondi Pavilion is Bondi’s beating heart for art and live events. Under its historic façade you’ll find rotating art exhibitions, theatre performances, dance workshops and community markets-ideal for staying dry and soaking up local culture. Check the Pavilion’s online calendar for same-day tickets and free entry slots.
2. Wander Through Bondi Pavilion Art Gallery & Waverley Library Galleries

Both gallery spaces showcase contemporary local and international art, often with interactive installations. Entry is free, and exhibitions change every few weeks-perfect for repeat visits. Don’t miss special pop-up talks or opening nights, where you can meet artists and enjoy light refreshments.
3. Join Family Fun Days & Indoor Festivals

When wet weather hits, Waverley Council often shifts outdoor festivals into Pavilion courtyards or community halls. Their Family Fun Day series features kids’ craft zones, storytelling, and pop-up food stalls-all under cover. Follow Council socials for last-minute wet-weather venue updates.
4. Catch a Movie at Westfield Bondi Junction

Just a 5-minute bus or walking ride north, Westfield Bondi Junction’s state-of-the-art cinemas screen the latest blockbusters. Popcorn, heated seats and fully licensed bars make it the ultimate escape when raindrops start to fall.
5. Take a Bracing Dip at Bondi Icebergs Pool

Believe it or not, Bondi Icebergs is open rain or shine. Their iconic ocean-fed saltwater pool offers uninterrupted sea views, even in drizzle. Warm up afterward in the sauna or grab a hot drink at the 9th Lane Café overlooking the surf.
6. Unwind with Yoga & Fitness Classes

Bondi’s wellness scene thrives indoors, too. Studios like White Lotus Yoga and BodyMindLife run beginner-friendly classes daily-choose from hatha yoga, pilates, and barre to keep the endorphins flowing when it’s grey outside.
7. Discover the Bondi Beach Graffiti Wall

Sheltered by overhanging awnings and beachfront promenades, the ever-changing graffiti wall near Campbell Parade is a colourful, rain-proof photo op. Local and international street artists leave fresh murals monthly-bring an umbrella and explore this open-air gallery.
8. Shop on Gould Street & Bondi Junction

From surf boutiques and designer pop-ups to handmade jewellery, Gould Street’s laneways are a treasure trove of indoor retail. For bigger brands and food courts, head upstairs at Westfield Bondi Junction. Retail therapy is the perfect antidote to a grey sky.
9. Indulge in Cozy Cafés & Day Spas

Bondi’s café culture shines in the rain-think single-origin lattes, artisan pastries, and hearty bowls by floor-to-ceiling windows. When you need extra pampering, book a deep-tissue massage or facial at spas like Gwinganna Bondi or Endota.
10. Embrace the Coastal Walk in Misty Skies

A light drizzle transforms the Bondi to Coogee Walk into a moody coastal spectacle. Rugged cliffs, pounding surf and dramatic skies make for unforgettable photos. Don a waterproof jacket, grab a takeaway coffee, and let the rain-washed ocean vistas inspire you.
11. Relax in the Turkish & Hot Sea Water Baths

Hidden inside the Pavilion are the historic Turkish and Hot Sea Water Baths-a nod to 1930s wellness trends. Warm mineral pools and steam rooms are open to all, offering a soothing retreat when Bondi’s waters feel too chilly.
Wet Weather Tips & FAQs
Check Live Updates: Waverley Council’s Wet Weather Line (9083 8305) and social feeds post venue closures, relocations and event changes .
Public Transport: Buses 333, 380 & 379 run from Bondi Junction station to Bondi Beach-perfect when rain makes parking scarce.
Dry Gear: Pack a lightweight raincoat and waterproof backpack; indoor venues are often a short stroll apart.
Early Birds & Night Owls: Many galleries and cafés open from 8 am; cinemas and spas run late, so you can tailor your day around the showers.
Rain or shine, Bondi’s got you covered. Bookmark this guide, duck into any of these spots, and discover a different side of Sydney’s most iconic beach-even on the wettest of days.

blocks.text: Children are welcome at Bondi Icebergs. While the iconic 50 m saltwater lap pool takes centre stage, there’s also a purpose-built children’s pool and full lifeguard coverage to keep your little ones safe and smiling .
1. Dedicated Kids’ Pool
Size & Depth: The kids’ pool is a shallow 25 m pool set at right angles to the main lap pool. It’s just deep enough for confident young swimmers without the worry of deep water .
Ocean-Fed Saltwater: Like the main pool, it fills with fresh surf water at high tide-so expect that bracing ocean chill! .
Shared Access: Adults may accompany very young children in the kids’ pool, making it perfect for a first swim together.
2. Safety & Lifeguards
Qualified Guards On Duty: Throughout opening hours, professional Waverley Council lifeguards patrol the pool deck and surrounding areas, ready to assist at a moment’s notice.
Pool Rules: Follow the “keep left” rule on swim lanes, and always supervise children under 12 within arm’s reach.
Emergency Equipment: Rescue boards, ring buoys and first-aid kits are strategically located around the pool.
3. Swim School & Lessons
Icebergs Swim School: For beginners aged 5–9, Bondi Icebergs runs dedicated 30-minute lessons in the children’s pool. Lessons cover water confidence, stroke basics and safety skills.
Holiday Intensives: Intensive programs run during school holidays; swimmers must pass a simple assessment before enrolling.
4. Entry Fees & Opening Hours
Daily Admission: Non-member children (under 16) $6, adults $9. Members enjoy discounted rates or free entry.
Year-Round Access: Mon–Fri: 6:00 am–6:30 pm
Sat–Sun: 6:30 am–6:30 pm
Thursdays: Closed for pool cleaning.
5. Tips for Families
Bring Layers: Even on warm days, the water can dip to 16 °C in winter-pack towels and warm clothes.
Arrive Early on Weekends: Parking and seating fill fast; early birds snag prime spots.
Snacks & Hydration: The café at pool level offers light bites and hot drinks-no outside food is permitted.
Sun Safety: Slip on a rashie, slop on sunscreen (SPF 30+), slap on a hat and slide on sunglasses between swims.
Bondi Icebergs Family FAQ
Can toddlers use the kids’ pool?
Yes, but they must be accompanied in the water by a responsible adult at all times.
Are arm-floaties allowed?
Only U – type life jackets are permitted; inflatable arm bands and noodles are not.
Is the kids’ pool heated?
No-the pool runs on unheated ocean water year-round.
Do I need to pre-book children’s lessons?
Yes, spots fill quickly. Book via the Icebergs Swim School page online after your child’s initial assessment.

title: Bondi Rescue: 20 Behind-the-Scenes Facts
metaDescription: 20 things you didn't know about Bondi Rescue - how it's filmed, whether it's staged, and what really happens behind the scenes at Bondi Beach.
h1: Behind The Scenes At Bondi Rescue: 10 things you may not know about the show
intro: Behind The Scenes At Bondi Rescue: 10 things you may not know about the show — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach Behind The Scenes At Bondi Rescue: 10 things you may not know about the show Bondi Rescue has been capturing the drama and heroism of Australia’s most famous beach lifeguards for nearly two decades

blocks.text: Bondi Rescue has been capturing the drama and heroism of Australia’s most famous beach lifeguards for nearly two decades. While viewers know the adrenaline-fuelled rescues, here are some behind-the-scenes tidbits and curiosities you might not have noticed.

Created by a Lifeguard The show was conceived by part-time Bondi lifeguard Ben Davies, who teamed up with producer Michael Cordell. Their insider perspective ensured the series felt authentic from episode one .

Narrated by a Reality TV Host Instead of a newsreader, Bondi Rescue is voiced by Osher Günsberg (formerly Andrew G), best known for hosting The Bachelor Australia. His warm, colloquial style adds a relatable tone to each rescue scenario .

Iconic Theme Song “In the Summertime” by Australian rock band Thirsty Merc isn’t just catchy-it perfectly captures Bondi’s laid-back vibe. The opening riff has become synonymous with sun, surf and lifesaving drama .

Record-Breaking Rescue Numbers Over a single summer season, the lifeguards perform roughly 5,000 rescues, tackling everything from rip currents to bluebottle stings. That’s an average of nearly 30 emergencies per day .

A Short-Lived Bali Spin-Off In 2008 Bondi Rescue: Bali sent the same team to Kuta Beach-but the nine-part series was pulled after just four episodes due to poor ratings, making it one of TV’s quickest cancellations .

Annual Ironman Challenge Each winter, the guards race in a handicapped Ironman: a 1 km run to Tamarama, 1 km ocean swim to Bronte, then a 2 km paddle back. It tests fitness and strategy, with elite athletes starting last to keep the contest tight .

Mid-Season Fitness Trials Beyond the Ironman, lifeguards undergo brutal mid-year trials: an 800 m pool swim in under 13½ minutes, 600 m surf swim, two 600 m sand runs, 600 m board paddle and timed rescue simulations-all within 25 minutes .

Star Power on the Sand Over the years Bondi’s HQ has hosted guest appearances by celebrities like David Hasselhoff, Russell Crowe, Paris Hilton, Conan O’Brien, Steve Irwin & daughter Bindi, Snoop Dogg and even the Indian Cricket Team .
Logie Award Winner The series took home the Logie for Most Popular Factual Program five years running (2008–2012), cementing its status as Australia’s favourite surf lifesaving show .

Global Reach & Revenue Bondi Rescue airs in over 180 countries. Cordell Jigsaw Productions pays Waverley Council an access fee to film on Bondi Beach, and individual lifeguards earn separate licensing fees for their on-camera appearances .

From its humble beach-side beginnings to international success, Bondi Rescue is packed with surprises beyond the dramatic dashes into the surf. Next time you watch, keep an ear out for Osher’s quips and an eye open for celebrity cameos!

blocks.text: Bondi’s sun-drenched sands, coastal walks and laid-back vibe have given rise to one of Sydney’s most vibrant café scenes. From Mediterranean-inspired small plates to towering pancake stacks and ethically sourced espresso, there’s something for every palate. Whether you’re fuelling up pre-swim or unwinding over avocado smash at sunset, this curated ranking will help you hop to the best Bondi cafés-complete with addresses, signature dishes and insider tips.
1. Blackwood
Address: Shop 3/87–89 Glenayr Ave, Bondi Beach

This upmarket brunch spot from the team behind Blackwood Cronulla brings Michelin-star-trained finesse to every dish. Expect truffled chilli scrambled eggs, blueberry-ricotta hotcakes and the cult-favourite “spicy bae roll,” all served with inventive drinks like coconut-lychee matcha and biscoff lattes. With a seasonal Mediterranean-Asian menu and doors opening at 7 am daily, it’s best to arrive early if you want a front-row seat.
2. Speedos Café
Address: 126 Ramsgate Ave, North Bondi

Dubbed “Bondi’s most Instagrammable café,” Speedos pairs beachfront views with colourful pancake towers, smoothie bowls and giant salads. The menu leans health-forward-think açai, fresh-pressed juices and clean eats-yet doesn’t skimp on flavour. Claim a window bench for sweeping ocean panoramas, then dive into their signature berry pancakes or avocado smash. It’s the perfect post-surf pick-me-up.
3. Makaveli
Address: 177, 2/179 Glenayr Ave, Bondi Beach

By day Makaveli is a laid-back café whipping up Brickfields pastries, focaccia slices and burrata on sourdough; by night it transforms into a buzzy cocktail bar. Try their chilli-tequila breakfast margarita and sample loaded sourdough toasts before returning for dinner share-plates. Weekly events-from pasta nights to bottomless brunch-keep locals coming back.
4. Pocket
Address: 266 Campbell Parade, Bondi Beach

From the makers of Makaveli, Pocket commands a corner spot with indoor-outdoor seating spilling onto Campbell Parade. Start with the bacon-egg “bae roll” on a milk bun, or choose Sonoma sourdough topped with whipped ricotta. Later, their dinner menu flips to raw kingfish, beef tartare and steak frites. Coffee, juices and dawn-till-dusk cocktails round out the experience.
5. Up South
Address: 249 Bondi Road, Bondi

Viral café queen Cherry Yap’s Up South is known for playful matcha creations-think cookie-croissant matcha, pistachio latte and banana-pudding-inspired blends. Daily-baked biscoff cookies and experimental biscuits line the treats cabinet, while a seasonally rotating hot food menu features shakshuka and loaded toasties. Snap a pic for the ‘Gram, then savour one of Sydney’s best strawberry matcha lattes.
6. Glory Days
Address: Bondi Pavilion, Queen Elizabeth Drive, Bondi Beach

Nestled within the iconic Bondi Pavilion, Glory Days serves an all-day menu against uninterrupted beach views. Breakfast burritos, açai bowls, prawn tacos and even vodka pasta invite hungry beachgoers in, while post-run rooftop raves add a dose of party energy. Grab takeaway and claim a sun lounger on the sand, or dine under their signature cream-and-toffee umbrellas.
7. Porch and Parlour
Address: 17–18/110 Ramsgate Ave, North Bondi

A decade-old staple, Porch and Parlour champions local produce on its custom Porch Ceramics. Don’t miss the pea pancakes with avocado, feta, snow pea sprouts and nut-seed crumble. Fresh juices and smoothies keep things light, while mimosas and Bloody Marys add weekend brunch flair. Dog-friendly and always buzzing, it’s a reliable neighbourhood haunt.
8. Chapter One
Address: 34 Campbell Parade, Bondi Beach

Directly opposite the waves, Chapter One combines café and wine-bar vibes. Since 2012 it has dished up gourmet breakfasts-think organic açai bowls, eggy bagels and blockbuster burgers-alongside artisanal coffee. Sip your flat white as lifeguards prep for the day, then stick around for their evening wine list and small plates.
9. Harry’s Bondi
Address: 2/136 Wairoa Ave, Bondi Beach

Once a hole-in-the-wall espresso bar, Harry’s now dazzles with a full food menu and inventive “H” canned drinks. Feast on prawn omelettes with fermented chilli butter or smashed croissants with smoked ham and mozzarella. The real draw? Dairy-free smoothies in PB&J and triple-berry matcha flavours-perfect for a sugary kick.
10. Bills
Address: 79 Hall Street, Bondi Beach

Bill Granger’s iconic Sydney institution landed in Bondi in 2014, bringing its fluffy scrambled eggs, sweet corn fritters and ricotta hotcakes to the sand. The airy, light-filled dining room complements the menu’s fresh simplicity-and don’t skip the honeycomb butter-topped hotcakes. With a dinner offering and coffee that’s consistently spot-on, Bills remains a must-visit.
Insider Tips for Café-Hopping in Bondi
Go Early or Late: Beat the queues by arriving at opening (7 am–8 am) or after 2 pm.
Weekdays > Weekends: For a more relaxed vibe, visit Tuesday–Thursday.
Mix & Match: Pair a beachfront spot (Speedos, Chapter One) with a hidden gem (Up South, Blackwood).
Bring Reusables: Many cafes offer discounts for reusable cups and containers.
Stay Hydrated: Bondi sun and coffee headiness call for regular water breaks!

blocks.text: If you’re dreaming of silky woodfired bread, creamy burrata, and sun-drenched courtyard dining, you’re not alone-Totti’s Bondi is one of Sydney’s most coveted dining experiences. But with its massive popularity, landing a table can feel like winning the lottery.
Here’s everything you need to know about how to get a booking at Totti’s Bondi-plus a few insider tips to help you beat the crowds.
Why Is Totti’s Bondi So Popular?

Totti’s isn’t just a restaurant; it’s an institution. Set behind The Royal Hotel on Bondi Road, Totti’s offers a laid-back, Mediterranean-inspired menu featuring handmade pastas, woodfired bread, and fresh, vibrant share plates. Combined with its sunny courtyard and beachy Bondi vibe, it’s no wonder it books out weeks in advance.
How to Book a Table at Totti’s Bondi
1. Book Online Early
Totti’s releases reservations online via Merivale’s booking site . Bookings open 30 days in advance at midnight (Sydney time), and prime lunch and dinner slots often get snapped up within minutes.
Tip: Set a calendar reminder and be ready to click right at midnight to increase your chances.
2. Be Flexible With Times
If you’re happy to dine at an earlier (think 11:30 am) or later sitting (after 8:30 pm), you’ll have a much better chance of getting a table. Off-peak times also mean a more relaxed atmosphere.
3. Try for Walk-Ins
Totti’s keeps limited tables available for walk-ins every day. To boost your walk-in chances:
Arrive right at opening time (usually from 11:30 am).
Midweek visits (especially Tuesday and Wednesday) are less competitive.
Smaller groups (2–3 people) are easier to accommodate.
4. Consider Dining Solo or as a Pair
Single diners or pairs sometimes get lucky at the bar or courtyard, where seating is more flexible. Plus, you’ll still get the full Totti’s experience-just without the wait.
5. Call Ahead if It’s Last-Minute
Sometimes there are cancellations, especially if the weather turns bad (as Bondi’s vibe is so outdoor-focused). It’s worth calling Totti’s directly the morning of your desired date to check.
6. Keep an Eye on Special Events and Pop-Ups
Occasionally, Totti’s hosts special events or off-site pop-ups where bookings are easier to score. Signing up for Merivale’s newsletter and following Totti’s on Instagram gives you early notice.
Quick Booking Summary:
Booking Platform: Merivale
Booking Release: 30 days in advance at midnight.
Walk-ins: Available (limited).
Best Days for Walk-ins: Tuesday and Wednesday.
Phone Number: +61 2 9114 7371
Final Tips for Visiting Totti’s Bondi
Arrive Early: Even with a booking, arriving early is a good move to soak up the atmosphere.
Order the Bread: It’s practically mandatory-Totti’s woodfired bread is a Sydney icon.
Leave Room for Dessert: Their tiramisu is worth saving space for.

blocks.text: Whale watching at Bondi Beach is a spectacular experience that combines Sydney’s iconic coastal scenery with the awe-inspiring sight of migrating whales. From May to November, Bondi becomes a prime location to witness humpback whales-and occasionally southern right whales-as they journey along Australia’s east coast. Here’s your comprehensive guide to making the most of whale watching at Bondi Beach.
🐋 When to Go: Whale Watching Season
Peak Season: May to November.
Northbound Migration: May to August.
Southbound Return: September to November, often with calves.
Best Times of Day: Early morning and late afternoon offer optimal lighting and calmer seas for spotting whales.
Weather Tips: Clear, calm days provide better visibility. Rough seas can make spotting whales challenging. On such days, consider returning when conditions improve.
📍 Top Land-Based Whale Watching Spots Near Bondi
Ben Buckler Point Located at the northern end of Bondi Beach, this elevated headland offers panoramic ocean views, making it a prime spot for whale watching.
Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk This scenic 6 km trail features multiple vantage points along the cliffs, providing excellent opportunities to spot whales during their migration.
Waverley Cemetery Clifftop Situated along the coastal walk, this area offers unobstructed views of the ocean, ideal for whale spotting.
Clovelly Beach & Gordons Bay These quieter spots along the coastal walk provide serene settings for whale watching, away from the larger crowds.
🚤 Whale Watching Cruises Departing Near Bondi
While there are no whale watching cruises departing directly from Bondi Beach, several operators offer tours from nearby locations:
Fantasea Cruising
Departure Point: Darling Harbour.
Duration: 2.5 hours.
Highlights: High-speed vessels reach the open ocean quickly, maximizing whale watching time. Features include outdoor viewing decks, climate-controlled cabins, and informative commentary.
Captain Cook Cruises
Departure Point: Circular Quay.
Duration: Approximately 2-3 hours.
Highlights: Offers morning and afternoon departures with options for breakfast or lunch onboard.
🧭 Tips for Successful Whale Watching
Bring Binoculars: Enhance your ability to spot whales from shore.
Stay Patient: Whale sightings can be sporadic; give yourself ample time.
Look for Signs: Watch for spouts, breaches, and tail slaps indicating whale presence.
Dress Appropriately: Wear layers and sun protection, as coastal weather can change rapidly.
Respect Wildlife: Maintain a safe distance and avoid disturbing the whales.

Whether you choose to watch from the cliffs or embark on a cruise, Bondi Beach offers unforgettable whale watching experiences. Plan your visit during the migration season, and you’re likely to witness these majestic creatures in their natural habitat.

Hotel Ravesis Hotel Ravesis reigns supreme with its flamingo-pink facade, multiple terraces and SoCal-inspired interiors. Downstairs, enjoy ice-cold schooners or a crisp rosé on tap post‐swim; upstairs, dive into neon-lit dancefloors and booming house DJs. Four distinct drinking zones-from the side balcony to the front terrace overlooking the surf-ensure every mood is covered, whether you’re hunting for a low-key beer or a late-night vodka lime and soda. Open until the early hours on weekends, Ravesis is the ultimate Bondi party palace, where the ocean breeze meets nightclub glamour.

Promenade Bondi Beach (Front Yard Bar) Housed in the heritage-listed Bondi Pavilion, Promenade’s Front Yard Bar blends coastal grandeur with casual charm. Festoon lights, comfy lounge seating and outdoor heaters set the scene for sunset spritzes and live DJs spinning chilled beats. The cocktail menu-served in mason jars and tiki glasses-features beach-inspired creations like the coral-hued “Sunnyboy Spritz,” while share plates such as wood-fired flatbreads and sambal-glazed skewers keep the party fueled. Whether you’re winding down after a day of surfing or rallying for an all-nighter, Promenade delivers unrivalled ocean views and a vibrant, inclusive atmosphere.

The Beaver Dining Parlour Bar Bondi’s beloved dive bar is all about good times and great booze. Neon signage and vintage film posters set a playful tone, while American-style burgers and loaded fries star alongside a mezcal-focused cocktail list. With cheap schooners on tap and themed nights-from 90s disco to pub quiz-this irreverent spot never takes itself too seriously. Open until late, the Beaver offers a carefree environment for group celebrations and spontaneous dance-offs. It’s proof that sometimes Bondi’s most memorable nights happen in the quirkiest, most unpretentious venues.

The Shop & Wine Bar By day, this Curlewis Street café is all about flat whites and sandwiches; by night, it transforms into an intimate wine bar with exposed brick walls and vintage leather armchairs. The carefully curated wine list spotlights boutique Australian and European labels, perfectly paired with artisanal cheese boards, charcuterie platters and house-pickled olives. Soft jazz drifts through the snug space, inviting lingering conversations and relaxed rendezvous. Ideal for date nights, The Shop & Wine Bar remains fiercely popular with locals who prize both its rare drops and its warm, after-hours ambiance.

Curly Lewis Brewing Co Bondi’s first microbrewery-bar, Curly Lewis, brings bespoke ales right to Campbell Parade. Massive stainless-steel tanks pump out everything from a tropical Bondi Hazy Ale to a sour Berry Bomb, all brewed in-house by founder Scotty Morgan and mates. Pair your pint with bar snacks like smashed beef burgers, loaded nachos or salt-and-pepper squid. Communal high tables and a beer-garden vibe encourage casual mingling, while fairy lights twinkle overhead at night. For craft-beer aficionados wanting a taste of Bondi’s DIY spirit, Curly Lewis is an essential stop.

The Beach Road Hotel Just steps from the foreshore, this sprawling pub offers multiple indoor and outdoor bars-including a sunny courtyard with DJs on weekends. Sink an ice-cold schooner or try a blood-orange negroni as you gather around rustic timber tables. Trivia nights, karaoke and live sports broadcasts keep the vibe buzzing seven nights a week. With friendly service and a menu of pub classics (from parmas to steaks), the Beach Road Hotel epitomizes laid-back Bondi charm. It’s where locals and visitors alike converge for casual drinks and good-humored revelry.

Bondi Bowling Club Bondi Bowlo has evolved from its 1935 roots into a modern club bar with stylish interiors and an enviable beer garden. Members (and their guests) feast on hearty share plates-think loaded fries and crispy chicken wings-between barefoot lawn-bowls sessions. A rotating tap list features local craft beers and house cocktails, while regular live music and DJ sets bring extra energy. With ocean breezes drifting through the clubrooms, Bondi Bowlo offers a unique blend of sport, snacks and spritzes that’s quintessentially Bondi.

The Corner House Housed in a former Denham Street tram stop, The Corner House marries rustic Italian share plates with a refined cocktail program upstairs. Downstairs, enjoy Mediterranean-inspired pizzas and wines by the bottle; head upstairs for spritzes with native finger lime, negronis with house-made vermouth and cozy lounge seating overlooking Bondi Road. Salvaged railway tracks and ferry pews nod to the site’s transport heritage, while regular live music fills the warm, communal space. With its blend of history and hospitality, The Corner House remains a neighbourhood favorite.

Makaveli Bar Tucked behind Glenayr Avenue, Makaveli flips from sunlit café to sultry cocktail den at dusk. Industrial-chic interiors of exposed brick and bespoke light fittings set a moody tone for sipping house-infused tipples like the chilli-tequila “Makaveli Marg” or lemongrass gin “Willowdene.” Italian-leaning small plates-stracciatella crostini, kingfish crudo-complement the drinks, while natural wines rotate weekly. Its extended hours (6 AM–11 PM) make Makaveli a versatile spot for both morning coffee and late-night negronis, appealing to a creative, loyal crowd.

Bondi Hardware One of the suburb’s original bar-restaurant mashups, Bondi Hardware on Hall Street delivers creative share plates and cocktails in industrial-chic surroundings. Exposed brick walls, metal beams and lush greenery create a vibrant, modern atmosphere. The cocktail list spans classics-like espresso martinis-to inventive house mixes featuring native botanicals. Shareable dishes (wood-roasted oysters, charred octopus, sangria jugs) fuel long nights under live DJ sets. With its perfect blend of design, drinks and dynamic programming, Bondi Hardware remains a cornerstone of Bondi’s nightlife.

Whether you’re craving craft beer at Curly Lewis or ocean-view cocktails at Promenade, these ten venues showcase the diversity and energy of Bondi Beach’s bar scene. Raise a glass, explore local flavors, and experience Bondi after dark in style.

blocks.text: Bondi Beach isn’t just sun, sand, and surf-its dining scene rivals its coastal charm with world-class eateries. After scouring top editorial rankings (Time Out , Urban List ) and hundreds of TripAdvisor reviews , we’ve distilled the 10 absolute must-visit restaurants in Bondi. From iconic cliff-side fine dining to casual taco joints, these spots promise unforgettable flavors by the ocean. Whether you crave a leisurely long lunch or a lively group feast, our ranking will guide you to the best tables in Bondi-read on and prepare to book that reservation!
1. Sean’s Panorama

Sean’s Panorama, an iconic 45-seat fine-dining restaurant on Campbell Parade, has been a Bondi institution since 1993. Chef-owner Sean Moran changes the menu daily, sourcing produce from his own Bilpin farm and other ethical growers around NSW. The restaurant’s floor-to-ceiling windows frame stunning north-facing views of Bondi Beach and the North Bondi Surf Life Saving Club. Guests rave about signature dishes like roast free-range chicken and seasonal seafood creations, all served in a relaxed, homely atmosphere. Reservations are essential for weekend long lunches with a Brisbane Spritz in hand.
2. Promenade Bondi Beach

Promenade Bondi Beach occupies the historic Bondi Pavilion, spanning multiple dining areas from a casual kiosk to the ocean-facing “Front Yard” terrace. Under Culinary Director Stephen Seckold, the menu draws inspiration from coastal flavors worldwide, with standout dishes like sambal-glazed toothfish skewers and coral trout crudo. The private “Grotto” dining room offers an intimate setting, while the sunny verandah is perfect for cocktails at sunset. Don’t miss the Sunnyboy Spritz-a playful nod to Aussie summertime-alongside fresh oysters and housemade pasta. Whether you’re here for a casual fish ‘n’ chips from the kiosk or a multi-course tasting menu, Promenade delivers a Bondi dining experience with white-sand views.
3. Totti’s

Totti’s is a casual Italian gem tucked behind The Royal on Bondi Road, known for its convivial, family-style atmosphere. Executive Chef Mike Eggert crafts a menu of hearty antipasti, Josper-grilled seafood, and housemade pastas that celebrate woodfire cooking. The restaurant’s leafy courtyard proves a popular spot for long lunches with a glass of local rosé. Their signature Neapolitan ice cream sandwich and famous wood-fired bread-served hot and smoky-are essential to the Totti’s experience. Despite its unassuming facade, Totti’s regularly sells out, so booking ahead is a must.
4. Mami’s

Mami’s is a vibrant, casual Mexican cantina on Bondi Road that feels plucked from the streets of Mexico City. Their taco selection-spiced chicken tinga, slow-cooked pork carnitas, rich beef birria, and chorizo-is stuffed into soft corn tortillas with fresh salsas. Burritos, nachos, and vegan-friendly options ensure there’s something for everyone, all priced under $20 and perfect for beachside feasting. The bright blue doors lead into a cheerful dining room where BYO beer and wine keep costs low. With quick service and BYO deals at The Royal across the street, Mami’s makes authentic Mexican the go-to lunch spot in Bondi.
5. Icebergs Dining Room and Bar

Icebergs Dining Room and Bar sits dramatically on the southern cliffs of Bondi, overlooking the namesake pool and the Pacific Ocean. Co-founded by hospitality legend Maurice Terzini in 2002, it offers a high-end, modern Italian menu that changes with the seasons. Signature dishes include a salt-crusted 150-day grain-fed rib eye, Koshihikari risotto, and decadent lobster spaghetti, plus a refined opera cake for dessert. Dining under the Gunyah pavilion or on the balcony feels like a private beach club-elevated and exclusive. Many guests opt for the $250 per person tasting menu to sample the full breadth of Icebergs’ culinary excellence.
6. North Bondi Fish

North Bondi Fish is literally beachfront-sand drifts through the door-as you dine on sustainably sourced seafood in a laid-back setting. Created by Matt Moran, the menu highlights Sydney rock oysters, kingfish ceviche, and crispy fish tacos alongside market-driven specials. Signature cocktails like the limoncello and yuzu spritz elevate the ocean views at this NoBo hotspot. The bright, airy dining room and outdoor seating attract brunch-goers and sunset crowds alike. Regulars swear by the fresh barramundi fillet and the witty pairing of seafood with zesty spritzers.
7. Fish Shop

Fish Shop reimagines the classic Aussie fish-and-chips with a fine-casual twist, using sustainably sourced ocean trout, salmon, and barramundi. Located steps from the shoreline, you choose your fish and pair it with housemade sauces like salsa verde or tangy aioli. Side dishes include freekeh salad with apricots and fagioli bianchi with herbs, elevating every bite beyond the usual floury chips. The minimalist dining room and efficient takeaway counter make it perfect for casual lunches after a morning swim. Whether dining in or grabbing fish to cook at home, Fish Shop consistently delivers fresh flavors and a Mediterranean mood.
8. Da Orazio

Da Orazio is a Hall Street institution celebrated for its contemporary Italian fare and legendary focaccia con porchetta sandwich. Chef Orazio D’Elia’s light and fragrant pizza bases frame woodfired porchetta, fresh vegetables, and creamy cheeses in creative crostini and pizzas. The menu balances share plates-like fregola frutti di mare and charcuterie-with hearty mains such as rotisserie porchetta and rich risottos. The intimate dining room and private back grotto offer cozy spots for date nights, while the bar serves classic spritzes to match the sunset. Since its triumphant 2022 reopening, Da Orazio has become a must-visit for both locals and visitors seeking authentic but inventive Italian in Bondi.
9. Bills

Bill Granger’s Bills Bondi is a breakfast and brunch institution, famed for its silky scrambled eggs and fluffy ricotta hotcakes. Since launching in Bondi in 1993, Bills has maintained its friendly vibe-expect queues, but enjoy a quick turnaround and welcoming service. The menu extends beyond brekkie with roast cod for dinner, high-end schnitzels, and a range of fresh small plates. Smoothies, Bloody Marys, and peach Bellinis make sunrise over the beach even sweeter. With communal seating and open-kitchen energy, Bills perfectly captures Bondi’s laid-back yet lively dining scene.
10. China Diner

China Diner brings bold modern Cantonese and Southeast Asian flavors to Campbell Parade with a menu designed for groups. Expect prawn and black fungus wontons drizzled with black vinegar, chilli caramel pork belly, and classic kung pao chicken that packs a punch. Their extensive dim sum selection-siu mai, har gow, and buns-pairs well with share-style mains and family-style platters. The vibrant, lantern-lit dining room hums with chatter, making it a perfect spot for celebrations and casual dinners. Affordable banquet menus start at $45 per head, offering unbeatable value for the quality and boldness of each dish.

From beachfront fine dining at Icebergs to casual tacos at Mami’s, these top Bondi restaurants will elevate any beach day. Don’t wait-reserve now and dive into Bondi’s vibrant culinary scene. Let us know which of these hotspots steals your heart (and appetite)!

blocks.text: When Bondi’s sun-drenched sands fill up, nothing saps your beach day faster than endless laps around the block looking for a carpark. Visitors often spend upwards of 30 minutes circling nearby streets before finding a space . On peak summer weekends, public holidays and sunny Saturday mornings, paid and free bays alike vanish by 9 AM, leaving many beachgoers frustrated before they even hit the sand.
Why Parking at Bondi Beach Is a Challenge
High demand: Bondi draws thousands on sunny weekends, quickly filling both on-street and off-street spots .
Limited capacity: Residential streets have strict permit zones and two-hour time limits, squeezing availability .
Peak-time rush: Paid carparks often fill by 9 AM in summer and on public holidays, while free bays disappear even faster .
Top Free Parking Spots
Blair Street (north end of Blair Street)

A little-known 24-hour free parking zone on Blair Street sits just a six- to eight-minute walk from the northern end of Bondi Beach. Spaces are limited, so arriving before 10 AM on weekends will boost your chances .
Upper end of Hall Street
The upper stretch of Hall Street offers all-day free parking, though it’s a 12–15 minute walk from the sand. Locals know about these bays, so be prepared to circle once or twice before snagging one .
Best Paid Parking Options
Bondi Beach Parking Station (Queen Elizabeth Drive)

Located on Queen Elizabeth Drive, this is the largest and closest off-street carpark to the beach. It offers both short-term and long-term bays, but fills up quickly on busy days-arrive early to secure your spot .
Pacific Bondi Car Park (152 Curlewis Street)

Operated by Wilson Parking, this lot sits opposite the Pavilion and is open daily from 5:30 AM to 12:30 AM. Casual rates start at $10 per 30 minutes (capped at $60 per day), with online prepayment discounts from $6 .
The Hub Hall Street Car Park (61–79 Hall Street via O’Brien St)

Also run by Wilson Parking, The Hub offers undercover bays with casual rates of $8 per hour (7 AM–7 PM), weekend rates capped at $35 for stays over four hours, and a $10 night special (entry after 5 PM, exit by midnight) .
Park Avenue North Bondi

Just a short walk from the beach, this private lot on Park Avenue has a good number of bays. It’s slightly cheaper than beachside options but still fills early during peak periods-plan to arrive before 9 AM .
Insider Tips to Score a Spot
Arrive early or late: Beat the peak crush by arriving before 8:30 AM or after 4 PM on busy days .
Use park-and-ride: Park at Bondi Junction Station (ample bays) and catch the 333 or 380 bus to the beach .
Leverage real-time apps: Use Parkopedia, Wilson Parking or Parkhound to check bay availability and pre-book paid spots .
Know the signs: Watch for resident-only zones (white-curb signage) and yellow lines-fines at Bondi can exceed $120 .
Evening freebies: Queen Elizabeth Drive and Park Drive South become free after 7 PM-perfect if you’re here for dinner or a sunset event .

With strategic planning-early arrival, a quick check of parking apps, or a park-and-ride at Bondi Junction-you can spend less time circling and more time soaking up Bondi’s iconic sands and surf. Happy parking!

Whether you’re a local seeking something new or a visitor keen to explore Bondi’s hidden side, these nine unique experiences will take your Bondi Beach getaway from ordinary to extraordinary.
No Lights No Lycra Dance Party

Every Monday night, the Bondi Pavilion transforms into a pitch-black dance floor-no instructor, no choreography, just pulsating beats and total freedom. Lose yourself in the music and connect with fellow dancers under cover of darkness for an exhilarating start to the week.
Beachside Ice Skating Rink

Yes, you read that right. Each winter, an open-air ice rink pops up beside the Pavilion, letting you glide and spin with the ocean breeze at your back. It’s Australia’s only beachfront skating rink-cool fun for all ages.
Winter Dip at the Icebergs Ocean Pool

Join the century-old tradition of Sunday swims at Bondi Icebergs from May through September. Brave the invigorating cold water, then warm up in the club’s sauna or café-ideal for thrill-seekers and chilly-weather enthusiasts alike.
Sculpture by the Sea Coastal Art Walk

Every October–November, this free outdoor gallery stretches along the coastal path to Tamarama. Wander past over 100 large-scale sculptures by local and international artists, set against the dramatic backdrop of sea cliffs and crashing waves.
Bondi Aboriginal Walking Tours

Led by local Guringai–Darug elder Walangari, this cultural tour winds from North Bondi down to the Pavilion. Learn about Dreamtime stories, spot ancient rock carvings, sample native bush foods, and finish with a live didgeridoo performance on the sand.
Stand-Up Paddleboard Yoga (SUP Yoga)

Combine your yoga practice with the gentle bob of the ocean on a SUP board. Held in the calm southern pocket of Bondi Beach, these sunrise and sunset classes build core strength, balance-and the odd splash-against a spectacular coastal backdrop.
Freediving Taster Sessions

Dive beneath the surface without tanks on a beginner freediving course just off Bondi’s shores. Learn breath-hold techniques, proper fin use and safety skills, then experience the underwater world in a single, serene breath.
Sunset Cinema at Dolphin Court

When the days heat up, Bondi Pavilion’s Dolphin Court becomes an open-air cinema mid-November to late December. Grab a bean bag, settle in under the stars, and enjoy a curated mix of new releases and classic films-complete with sea breeze and salty air.
Scenic Seaplane Flight Over Bondi

For the ultimate aerial perspective, take a 15-minute seaplane hop from nearby Rose Bay. Soar over Bondi’s iconic curve, the rocky cliffs of the Eastern Suburbs and across Sydney Harbour for a once-in-a-lifetime photo-op-and a healthy dose of adrenaline.

Whether you’re dancing in the dark at No Lights No Lycra or soaring above Bondi’s coastline by seaplane, these adventures will give you a whole new appreciation for one of Australia’s most famous beaches. Pack your sense of adventure, book ahead where required, and discover Bondi’s best-kept secrets on your next visit!

blocks.text: Bondi Beach isn’t just Australia’s most iconic stretch of sand - it’s a global bucket-list destination. Whether you’re a local planning a weekend dip or a tourist seeking sun and surf, here are 8 essential things to know before you go.
1. Surf’s Up – For All Levels

Bondi Beach is a surfing haven, offering waves for beginners and pros alike. The southern end attracts experienced surfers with stronger breaks, while the northern end has gentler waves and is safer for swimming. Local surf schools offer lessons daily if you’re keen to learn.
2. Bondi Icebergs is a Must-See

The Bondi Icebergs Club, with its stunning ocean pool perched above crashing waves, is one of Sydney’s most photogenic spots. Established in 1929, it’s perfect for a swim or a meal with a view - and yes, non-members are welcome.
3. The Coastal Walk is Breathtaking

Don’t miss the 6-kilometre Bondi to Coogee walk. It weaves along dramatic cliffs, past beaches like Tamarama and Bronte, and offers panoramic ocean views and cafes for pit stops. It’s free, scenic, and one of Sydney’s best outdoor activities.
4. Bondi’s Food Scene is Buzzing

Bondi’s dining is as fresh as its sea breeze. Think beachfront cafes, organic brunches, and buzzing bars. Head to Hall Street and Curlewis Street for standout spots like Bills, Gelato Messina, and Bondi’s famous fish and chips.
5. Markets & Events Add Local Flavour

Sundays bring the Bondi Markets, where you’ll find artisan goods, vintage fashion, and street eats. In spring, “Sculpture by the Sea” transforms the coast into a clifftop art gallery - an unforgettable way to see Bondi.
6. Getting There is Easy
Bondi is accessible via several direct buses, including the popular 333 and 380 routes from the city and Bondi Junction. Parking can be tricky on weekends, so public transport is your best bet.
7. Plenty of Places to Stay
From the boutique QT Bondi to hostels and short-term rentals, there’s an option for every budget. Book early during summer and holidays, as Bondi accommodation fills fast.
8. Safety First – Swim Between the Flags

Bondi is patrolled daily by lifeguards, including the stars of Bondi Rescue. Always swim between the red and yellow flags, and check the surf conditions before diving in. The north end is generally calmer and more family-friendly.
Final Tip: Bondi is more than a beach - it’s a lifestyle. Come early for a sunrise swim, linger for lunch, and stay for the sunset glow over the cliffs. You won’t forget it.

With its golden sands, rolling surf, and lush parklands, it’s the perfect backdrop for a festive beachside gathering.
🎄 What to Expect on Christmas Day
🎉 A Multicultural Festive Crowd
Expect a lively and diverse crowd, with attendees donning Santa hats, reindeer antlers, and festive outfits. The atmosphere is electric, filled with music, laughter, and the spirit of togetherness.
🥪 Beach Picnics and Feasts
While barbecues may not be permitted, many bring picnic blankets and enjoy classic Aussie Christmas meals like prawns, salads, and chilled drinks. Remember, alcohol is prohibited on the beach.

Impromptu DJ setups and portable speakers are common, playing a mix of festive classics and dance hits. The energy remains high throughout the day, with spontaneous dance sessions and sing-alongs.

From beach volleyball to Frisbee, there’s no shortage of activities to keep you entertained. The grassy park area is also perfect for lounging, socializing, or setting up friendly competitions.

⏰ Arrive Early

Bronte Beach gets busy quickly on Christmas Day. Aim to arrive by mid-morning to secure a good spot on the sand or in the park. Parking is limited, so consider public transport or ride-sharing options.
🎒 Pack Smart
Sun Protection: Bring sunscreen, hats, sunglasses, and umbrellas for shade.
Beach Essentials: Towels, swimwear, and water shoes for exploring the rock pools.
Snacks and Drinks: Keep hydrated with plenty of water, and pack a festive picnic.
Trash Bags: Help keep the beach clean by carrying out your rubbish.
🚩Follow Local Rules
Alcohol is prohibited at Bronte Beach, so plan your beverages accordingly. Lifeguards are on duty, but always swim between the flags and follow safety guidelines.
🚨 Safety and Community Considerations

In recent years, the number of incidents at Bronte has increased, threatening the future of the event. While the day is overwhelmingly safe and festive in nature, whenever alcohol is involved, which it inevitably is, the risks do rise. Authorities have implemented measures such as increased ranger and police presence, additional waste management, and crowd control pathways to ensure safety and cleanliness.
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Who Should Attend?
Bronte Beach’s Christmas celebration is ideal for:
Expats and Travelers: Celebrate the holidays with fellow adventurers from around the world.
Groups of Friends: Gather your crew for a memorable day of fun, food, and festivities.
Solo Visitors: Don’t be shy-Christmas at Bronte is a welcoming event, and you’re bound to meet new friends.
For families, the more relaxed festivities at Bondi Beach might be preferable.
🌟 What Makes It Special?

The unique mix of cultures, the stunning beachside setting, and the joyful atmosphere make Bronte Beach a standout Christmas destination. Whether you’re looking to relax in the sun, make new friends, or simply enjoy a festive day by the ocean, this celebration offers something for everyone.
So, grab your Santa hat, pack your picnic, and head to Bronte Beach this Christmas for a holiday experience you’ll never forget. Cheers to celebrating the season in true Aussie style!

blocks.text: Massive waves have caused significant damage to the iconic Bondi Icebergs swimming pool in Sydney, with repair costs expected to run into the hundreds of thousands and the pool closed until April 18. Swells surged up to 10 metres above the pool deck, smashing 30 metres of glass fencing near the change rooms, warping railings, and hurling a 20-tonne water tank onto the beach. The nearly 100-year-old facility is now closed, likely for at least a week, as the extent of the destruction is assessed.

According to Bondi Icebergs Club general manager Bob Tate in media reports, the waves struck around midnight on Tuesday, coinciding with a high tide of 1.9 metres. The surf overwhelmed the pool deck and even tore through the lifeguard tower, which sits 10 metres above. CCTV captured the torrent sweeping through the office, scattering furniture and ripping cupboards from the walls.
“I’ve never seen anything like this,” Tate said. “It’s unbelievable.”

The club shut the pool on Tuesday afternoon-a rare move Tate says hasn’t happened in two decades-after waves rose two metres above the pool during low tide. Crews began cleaning debris, including shattered glass, from the site on Wednesday.

A guide. Bondi Beach and Bondi Junction are two distinct areas in Sydney, Australia. Whilst they are closely connected neighbouring suburbs

blocks.text: Bondi Beach and Bondi Junction are two distinct areas in Sydney, Australia. Whilst they are closely connected neighbouring suburbs, visitors to Sydney don’t typically realise how different the suburbs are before arriving.
Here are the key differences between the two:

Location - Bondi Beach is a coastal suburb located about 7 kilometres east of Sydney's central business district. Bondi Junction, on the other hand, is an inner-eastern suburb located about 6 kilometres east of the CBD, about 2km from Bondi Beach.

Environment - Bondi Beach is known for its stunning natural beauty, with a long stretch of white sand, crystal-clear waters, and dramatic cliffs. Bondi Junction, on the other hand, is more of an urban environment, with high-rise buildings, shopping centers, and other commercial developments.

Tourist destination - Bondi Beach is a world-renowned tourist destination, attracting visitors from around the globe. It's known for its surf breaks, beach culture, and vibrant atmosphere. Bondi Junction, on the other hand, is primarily a commercial hub, with several shopping centers, restaurants, and office buildings.

Transportation - Bondi Beach is accessible by several bus routes, as well as a train that runs to nearby Bondi Junction. Bondi Junction is a major transportation hub, with a train station, several bus stops, and a major interchange for local and regional transportation.

Lifestyle - Bondi Beach is known for its laid-back beach lifestyle, with a focus on health and wellness. Bondi Junction is more of a commercial area, with a focus on shopping, dining, and entertainment.

Overall, Bondi Beach and Bondi Junction offer two distinct experiences in Sydney. Bondi Beach is a world-famous tourist destination, while Bondi Junction is primarily a commercial hub. However, both areas offer a range of amenities and attractions for locals and visitors alike.

blocks.text: So you’ve survived the 14km City2Surf run from Sydney's CBD to Bondi Beach and now it’s time to rehydrate and celebrate your achievement. What's better than celebrating your accomplishment with fellow runners, supporters, and the vibrant local community?

We’ve listed our top picks of where to go post-race but be aware that all spots fill up quickly as tens of thousands of people stream into Bondi. By midday you can expect long queues so we recommend heading straight from the race to your preferred venue. Or, if coming just for the party, being at your venue by 11am at the latest to secure a spot without the massive wait.
Hotel Ravesis

The go-to pub for runners and their support crew in previous years this hotspot fills up quickly, and those premium balcony spots are always in high demand so don’t stop running when you reach the finish line, hotfoot it the extra 500m here.
Glory Days, Bondi Pavillion

P.E Nation is hosting AFTERGLOW, the ultimate City2Surf recovery party, on Sunday, 10 August at Glory Days in the Bondi Pavilion, just steps from the finish line. From 8:30am to 1:30pm, runners, supporters and the community can enjoy a mix of performance, wellness and celebration. The event will feature DJ duo Allias and Aura, plus wellness experiences from WelleCo and Dermalogica. Limited-edition AFTERGLOW T-shirts and foil blankets will be gifted to lucky attendees.
Royal Bondi

Always one of the best parties, the Merivale crew have partnered with Hahn and Byron Bay Brewery to shout every runner a congratulatory schooner of Hahn SuperDry or a peach & mango seltzer on arrival. Then the real party starts, with all-day DJs and entertainment from our fabulous host, the hilarious Jackie Daniels.
Beach Rd Hotel

Let’s face it, The Beachy knows how to throw a party and this is the biggest afterparty of them all. For those who have the legs to make it there you can’t go wrong with this option but be aware that the queue here also wins the prize as the biggest if you don’t hotfoot it there in quick time.
North Bondi Fish

Starting at 11am, runners will be treated to a free marg (book and attend wearing your race bib), DJs will take over with views of the legendary Bondi Beach, delivering the latest tunes until 3pm and an epic seafood bbq will take centre stage.
The Golden Sheaf

The Golden Sheaf will host City2Sheaf as a post-race venue for City2Surf participants and supporters. For the first time, doors will open at 8am, with activities running throughout the day. The venue will provide food, drinks, and entertainment, including a brunch-style menu suitable for post-race recovery. Beverages such as Balter XPA and a 2-for-$30 Vodka Red Bull special will be available. Complimentary massages will be offered by 3 Minute Angels, and DJs will perform in the courtyard and rooftop from 10am until late. Free shuttle buses will operate between Bondi and The Golden Sheaf on a first-come, first-served basis. Limited bookings can be made between 10am and 12pm, with most of the venue allocated to walk-ins.
Hotel Bondi
If your legs have seized up and walking is no longer and option Hotel Bondi may be a sensible choice. Close to the finish line, this place is always lively for a post-race celebration.
North Bondi RSL
Always one of the best places on Bondi for a beer, City2Surf is no exception. Open from 10am, head here for a relaxed beer.
