Imagine colourful kites of all shapes and sizes filling the sky, soaring gracefully above the golden sands of Bondi Beach. This awe-inspiring sight has been a tradition for over four decades, and it all began in 1978 when a group of wind energy enthusiasts decided to host a kite festival. Little did they know that their passion project would grow into one of the world’s most renowned kite flying events.
The Birth of a Legacy

At the heart of this festival is John Silk, a local from Glebe and a student at Sydney University, whose fascination with wind energy led him to fall in love with kite making and flying. Alongside his friends, they saw Bondi’s Springtime charm as the perfect backdrop for their dream. On September 10, 1978, they launched the first Festival of the Winds, with Mr. Ernie Page, the Mayor of Waverley at the time, officially opening the event.
Kite-Flying Extravaganza

Today, the Festival of the Winds is a delightful blend of professional kite flying exhibitions featuring national and international talent, alongside a cornucopia of entertainment and cultural experiences. Bondi Pavilion cultural staff add their touch to the festival by organizing food stalls, kite-making workshops, gallery exhibitions, and more.
Fun for All Ages

The Festival of the Winds is a true family affair. People of all ages can celebrate the joy of kite flying and even craft their own sky-high creations at one of the kite-making workshops. The day is filled with captivating demonstrations, and the main stage hosts a lively entertainment program that keeps spirits high.
Plan Your Visit

This year, don’t miss the chance to be part of this vibrant celebration. The Festival of the Winds is set to take place on Sunday, September 10th, at Bondi Beach. However, keep in mind that parking is limited, and roads will be closed, so it’s best to plan your journey using public transport for a smooth and stress-free experience.

As you gaze up at the myriad of kites soaring in the Bondi skies, you’ll feel a sense of wonder and unity with fellow festival-goers. The Festival of the Winds isn’t just about kites; it’s about reaching for the sky and embracing the beauty of Bondi Beach in a whole new way. So, mark your calendar and get ready to soar high at Bondi Beach’s Festival of the Winds.

blocks.text: When planning a trip to Sydney’s iconic Bondi Beach, timing can make all the . With its golden sands, vibrant surf culture, and lively atmosphere, Bondi is a must-visit destination any time of the year. However, understanding the nuances of Bondi Beach weather and the different Bondi seasons can help you make the most of your visit. Here’s your comprehensive seasonal guide to the best time to visit Bondi Beach.
Summer (December to February)
Why Visit in Summer?
Weather : Summer in Bondi Beach is characterized by hot, sunny days with average temperatures ranging from 20°C to 26°C (68°F to 79°F). The water is warm, perfect for swimming and surfing.
Events : This season is packed with events like the iconic Bondi Beach New Year’s Eve celebrations and the Bondi Open Air Cinema.
Crowd Levels : Expect large crowds as both locals and tourists flock to the beach to enjoy the sun. Early mornings or late afternoons are ideal times to find a spot on the sand.
Pros
Best beach weather.
Numerous events and activities.
Vibrant nightlife.
Cons
Crowded beaches.
Higher accommodation prices.
Autumn (March to May)
Why Visit in Autumn?
Weather : The weather remains warm and pleasant, with temperatures ranging from 17°C to 24°C (63°F to 75°F). The ocean is still warm enough for swimming.
Events : Bondi hosts the Festival of the Winds in September, showcasing beautiful kites from around the world.
Crowd Levels : Fewer tourists compared to summer, making it a great time to enjoy the beach with less congestion.
Pros
Pleasant weather.
Fewer crowds.
Lower accommodation costs.
Cons
Some businesses may reduce their hours post-summer.
Winter (June to August)
Why Visit in Winter?

Weather : Winter in Bondi Beach is mild, with temperatures ranging from 8°C to 17°C (46°F to 63°F). While swimming might be too chilly for some, it’s a great time for coastal walks and whale watching.
Events : Bondi Winter Magic Festival transforms the area with ice skating and cultural events.
Crowd Levels : Significantly fewer tourists, offering a peaceful experience.
Pros
Best time for whale watching.
Minimal crowds.
Unique winter events.
Cons
Cooler temperatures limit swimming and sunbathing.
Spring (September to November)
Why Visit in Spring?
Weather : Spring sees temperatures rising from 14°C to 22°C (57°F to 72°F), with blooming flowers and warmer seas.
Events : Sculpture by the Sea, held in November, is a world-renowned outdoor sculpture exhibition along the Bondi to Tamarama coastal walk.
Crowd Levels : Crowds begin to return, but it’s still less busy than summer.
Pros
Warm, pleasant weather.
Beautiful natural scenery.
Exciting cultural events.
Cons
Increasing crowds towards the end of spring.

The best time to visit Bondi Beach largely depends on your preferences. If you thrive in bustling, lively environments and love the heat, summer is your season. For those who prefer a quieter beach experience with mild weather, autumn and spring are ideal. Winter offers a unique charm with its mild climate and special events, perfect for a peaceful getaway.

No matter when you visit, Bondi Beach’s stunning scenery and vibrant culture will ensure an unforgettable experience. Plan according to the Bondi Beach weather and seasonal events to make the most of your trip.

blocks.text: Whale Watching in Bondi: The Ultimate Guide

Australia’s stunning coastline offers some of the best whale-watching opportunities in the world, and Bondi Beach is no exception. Located in Sydney's eastern suburbs, Bondi is famous for its golden sands and surf culture, but it’s also a fantastic spot to witness the majestic migration of whales. Here’s your guide to the best places to watch whales around Bondi and the ideal times to catch a glimpse of these magnificent creatures.
Why Bondi?

Bondi Beach is a prime location for whale watching due to its elevated coastal walkways, breathtaking ocean views, and accessibility. The annual migration of humpback whales along the east coast of Australia brings these giants close to the shore, providing spectacular viewing opportunities for locals and tourists alike.
Best Places to Watch Whales Around Bondi

Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk Description : This iconic walk stretches for about 6 km along the coast, offering numerous vantage points. The elevated cliffs and headlands provide panoramic views of the ocean, making it an ideal spot for whale watching.
Best Spots : Marks Park, Mackenzies Point, and the Clovelly Headland are particularly recommended. Marks Park even has dedicated whale-watching platforms.

Ben Buckler Point Description : Located at the northern end of Bondi Beach, Ben Buckler Point offers excellent views of the Pacific Ocean. Its elevated position makes it a perfect place to spot whales as they breach and play in the waters below.
Facilities : Ben Buckler Point has seating and open spaces, allowing for a comfortable and relaxed whale-watching experience.

Marks Park Description : Situated between Bondi and Tamarama beaches, Marks Park is a well-known whale-watching location. The park's headland provides an unobstructed view of the ocean, and it's not uncommon to see whales swimming close to the shore.
Facilities : The park features seating areas, walking paths, and informative signs about the whales and their migration patterns.
Best Time to See Whales
Whale watching in Bondi is best during the annual migration season. Here’s a breakdown of the optimal times to visit:

June to August : This period marks the northward migration of humpback whales from Antarctica to the warmer breeding grounds off the Queensland coast. During these months, you can see whales traveling close to the shore, often with calves in tow.

September to November : The southward migration occurs during these months, as the whales return to Antarctic waters with their new calves. This is a fantastic time to see the playful behavior of young whales learning to breach and slap their tails.
Tips for Whale Watching
Timing : Early morning and late afternoon are generally the best times to spot whales, as the ocean is often calmer, making it easier to see the whales' movements.
Equipment : Bring a pair of binoculars for a closer view, and a camera with a good zoom lens to capture the moments.
Patience : Whale watching requires patience. Spend some time at your chosen spot, and keep your eyes peeled on the horizon.
Weather : Check the weather forecast before heading out. Clear, calm days provide the best viewing conditions.

Bondi Beach and its surrounding coastal areas offer some of the best whale-watching spots in Sydney. Whether you choose the scenic Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk, the serene Ben Buckler Point, or the panoramic views of Marks Park, you’re in for an unforgettable experience. Remember to visit during the peak migration seasons and follow our tips to maximize your chances of seeing these incredible marine giants.
So, grab your binoculars, pack a picnic, and head to Bondi for a day of spectacular whale watching. It’s an experience that connects you with nature in the most magnificent way possible.

Their Bondi location is a testament to their global appeal, offering over 150 flavors of gelato, yogurt, and sorbet, all churned fresh daily. Anita’s philosophy is about blending traditional methods with modern twists, resulting in creamy, rich, and smooth textures. Their menu features a range of organic, sugar-free, and vegan options, catering to every palate and dietary preference. Favorites include Cookie Man, a dream for anyone with a sweet tooth, and their vegan Chocolate Sorbet, proving that indulgence can be guilt-free. blocks.text: Bondi Beach has long been a symbol of Sydney’s sublime coastal life. It’s not just a beach, but a lifestyle, attracting a multitude of locals and tourists alike. Yet, amidst its bustling cafes, vibrant street art, and the famous Bondi Icebergs pool, we often get asked about safety, from crime rates to swim risks. In a nutshell, Bondi is a safe place for local and tourists. The biggest safety threat is for those venturing into the ocean, underestimating the risks involved if you are not an experienced open water swimmer. This risk is magnified greatly for anyone who doesn’t swim between the red and yellow flags. Here, we take a look at the key questions raised about Bondi’s safety.
Crime Rates in Bondi

Bondi is generally considered a very safe suburb, boasting a community vibe where families, young professionals, and tourists coalesce. According to the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, the crime rates in Bondi have been relatively low and stable over the years. The most common offenses tend to be related to theft and minor property damage, not uncommon for areas popular among tourists.

However, as with any bustling urban area, it’s wise to remain vigilant. Nighttime can see a surge in activity, especially around bars and clubs, where instances of petty crime are more likely to occur. The local police force maintains a visible presence, and community initiatives often focus on fostering a safe and inclusive environment for all.
Pickpockets on the Beach

Bondi’s allure also attracts pickpockets and petty thieves, preying on distracted beachgoers. Tourists, often engrossed in the beach’s beauty or their relaxation, can become easy targets. Whilst the incidence of this occurring is very low, to counter this it’s advisable to minimise valuables brought to the beach and use lockers at the Pavillion for safe storage. Being mindful of your belongings and your surroundings can significantly reduce the risk of theft.

The local authorities and community groups often issue advisories and tips for tourists, emphasising the importance of vigilance. Beach patrols and surveillance also act as deterrents, but the primary defense against pickpockets is always personal awareness and precaution.
Swim Safety at Bondi

The azure waters of Bondi are inviting, but they also hold hidden dangers, primarily in the form of rips and currents. Bondi lifeguards, celebrated heroes of the beach, are well-trained to manage swim safety. They consistently advise swimmers to stay between the flags, marking the safest areas to swim.

Despite these measures, each year sees a number of rescues, often involving tourists or inexperienced swimmers underestimating the ocean’s power. To ensure safety, it’s crucial to understand and respect the beach’s conditions, adhere to lifeguard warnings, and avoid swimming alone or under the influence of alcohol.

In response to swim safety concerns, Bondi has implemented various educational programs aimed at increasing awareness about the ocean’s dynamics. These programs emphasize the importance of swimming in patrolled areas and understanding beach signage, contributing significantly to reducing incidents and ensuring a safe environment for all beachgoers.

Bondi Beach, with its blend of natural beauty and urban charm, continues to be a magnet for those seeking the quintessential Sydney experience. While its crime rates are relatively low, and efforts to ensure swim safety are robust, the key to a secure visit lies in personal responsibility. By staying vigilant, respecting the ocean’s might, and heeding local advice, visitors can fully embrace the joys of Bondi, making their experience not only memorable but also safe.

However, it’s important to note that even these renowned beaches are not immune to the occasional adverse impact of heavy rainfalls. Stormwater runoff can temporarily affect water quality, carrying pollutants into the ocean. Therefore, while Bondi and surrounding beaches maintain high standards of cleanliness, it is always wise for beachgoers to consult Beachwatch, especially after significant downpours. The website’s real-time updates and alerts ensure that swimmers are informed about the current water conditions, allowing them to avoid any temporary pollution and enjoy their beach time safely. This practice not only safeguards individual health but also fosters a collective responsibility towards maintaining the pristine nature of these beloved coastal areas.

One caveat on this would be the North Bondi kids ocean pool. With dozens of kids in there at any one time over summer this pool can become a little, let’s say, murky if the waves aren’t making it over the pool wall. It’s great for a kids splash but perhaps not the spot to teach them how to swim with their head underwater.

blocks.text: A guide to Australia Day at Bondi Beach - let’s tread carefully here as everyone has a (very strong) opinion on the day and its significance. Putting aside the politics of the day for a moment, if you can, let’s talk about what happens at Bondi on this Australian public holiday because the beach has traditionally been a magnet for visitors on the 26th of January with more than 100,000 visitors visiting on the day.

This day used to be the most festive of the year at the beach. Who could forget the hundreds of giant inflatable Haviana thongs (flip flops) or the free mangoes that were given to passers by throughout the day.

Whilst it is still a wonderful day out the festivities have been replaced by a large, generally jovial and relaxed crowd. You will find fewer flag-draped beachgoers, although there will still be some.
These days you will struggle to find any venues mentioning Australia Day in its event listings which is why we are providing this guide to assist you in planning your day.
Here are our tips for your day out at Bondi for the day.
Parking
Parking is at its worst on this day so we recommend you arrive early and set up for the day ahead.
Beach set up

Despite the huge crowds the good news is you will easily find space on the beach. Families can’t beat North Bondi whilst a little further south would be our pick for those who are kid-free. If you arrive later in the day, the middle of the beach will be the easiest spot to find space.
Police and rangers

There is always a strong ranger and police presence at the beach to help deal with the crowds and traffic, who are quick to hand out on-the-spot fines for littering and drinking alcohol at beaches and parks. Leave the alcohol at home and head to a nearby pub or bar in Bondi if you’re looking for a drink. And whatever you do, leave the antisocial behaviour behind as police are on incredibly high alert due to the tensions that exist around the day and have little tolerance for bad behaviour.
Eating and drinking

Unlike in years past no one is advertising Australia Day festivities. That said, we suggest heading to the Beach Rd Hotel, the Royal or the two RSLs if you are looking for good atmosphere on the day. The pavillion on the beach will also be a great spot for dining. Note that these venues will all fill up as the day progresses so consider your timing.

Further afield, the Clovelly Hotel is the top spot in the eastern suburbs for a party and The Sheaf in Double Bay has traditionally been fun as well. Bronte Beach is a good alternative to Bondi if you’re looking for something a little different.
Cultural Recognition

Waverley Council will be holding a Dawn Reflection to acknowledge the resilience and survival of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and their connection to Country and culture at 5:30am on the beach near the Pavilion.
Swim safety

Australia Day is notoriously tough for lifesavers with a combination of huge crowds, plenty of visitors who are Inexperienced in ocean water conditions, and occasional poor water conditions (swell, rips etc).

Whatever you do, please swim between the flags. Don’t get in the water beyond your knees if you can’t swim, and if you do find yourself in trouble remember to relax and float on your back, putting one arm in the arm for attention if that doesn’t affect your ability to float. And of course, don’t swim under the influence of drugs or alcohol.

h1: Everything you need to know about the Bondi Salties
intro: Everything you need to know about the Bondi Salties — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach Everything you need to know about the Bondi Salties If you’ve not heard of the Bondi Salties we’re certain you’ve seen them. This large community group of ocean swimming enthusiasts meet at 6.15am every Friday morning at t

blocks.text: If you’ve not heard of the Bondi Salties we’re certain you’ve seen them. This large community group of ocean swimming enthusiasts meet at 6.15am every Friday morning at the North Bondi ramp for a run followed by a swim across the bay. They always look like they’re having fun and ask anyone who has joined them and they will confirm that this is one of the best community groups in Sydney to be a part of - friendly, welcoming and supportive. We spoke to them to find out just what the Bondi Salties are all about.
How did it start?

One beautiful Friday morning in June 2013 a group of old friends led by Alister Dalzell decided to meet at the North Bondi Ramp for a quick soft sand, bay swim and coffee. Back on land, the post-swim smiles were large and the energy was electric…we were hooked and the Salties were born.
Who can join and how much does it cost?

We are a free community group and welcome all ocean swimming lovers. Important to note, however, that we do not provide any water safety during our swims. Every swimmer should be confident in navigating open water and able to swim 1km of continuous freestyle or more. A Bondi bay swim is 1.3kms.
What about tourists? Can they participate as a one off?
Of course! Once they’ve completed a swim they’ll be rewarded with the iconic yellow Salties swim cap courtesy of our partner Santa Vittoria. A bit of memorabilia to take home!
What makes the Salties different to other swimming clubs?
Consistency, the act of showing up every Friday - regardless of big or small swell, bad or good week, summer or winter. This consistency really embodies the group and the people.
Any particularly memorable moments over the years?

We turned 10 last year and hosted a birthday party at the North Bondi RSL for 200 Salt-loving humans. It was an awesome night and a great way to celebrate the milestone with old and new Salties. We also love a great dress-up/costume themed party…I mean who doesn’t!
How many dolphin encounters? Sharks?

Multiples of both. The dolphin encounters are special as you usually hear them before you see them; a truly magical experience. Sharks on the other hand usually pop up when you least expect; but are equally as magical. There are often small stingrays and fish hiding between the sand and waves, and these are fun to spot on your way out or into shore.
And we understand coffee plays a big role?

Coffee plays a HUGE role. The combination of the post swim high, caffeine and good company is very special. Being on a Friday folks also usually have more time to chat, sip coffee, and enjoy the morning salty glow.
Learn more about the Salties at their website here .

title: Waverley Park Playground, Bondi: Family Guide
metaDescription: Waverley Park playground in the heart of Bondi - one of Sydney's best. What's there for kids, shade, toilets and why families love it.
h1: Waverley Park Playground: Sydney’s best playground in the heart of Bondi
intro: Waverley Park Playground: Sydney’s best playground in the heart of Bondi — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach Waverley Park Playground: Sydney’s best playground in the heart of Bondi The newly revamped Waverley Park Playground in Bondi is a standout destination for families, widely described as Sydney’s best p

blocks.text: The newly revamped Waverley Park Playground in Bondi is a standout destination for families, widely described as Sydney’s best playground right now.

Finalised in late 2023 and designed to celebrate the park’s history, a modern rocket ship and launch tower centrepiece pays tribute to the original 1960s built space. In a recent press release the council described the rocket ship as a “modern interpretation of the park’s original rocket ship that was installed in the 1960s and is fondly remembered by generations of families”.

Now this is no ordinary rocket ship, featuring a launch button that sends “steam” (water vapour) pouring out of the rocket giving the impression of it blasting off, a “control panel” featuring knobs, dials and lights that kids can take charge of and a challenging but relatively safe climbing apparatus for kids to navigate their way to the top before clambering across to the giant slide.

The rocket is just the beginning. The playground is one of those rare examples that is truly designed for kids of all ages offering diverse play areas that cater to children of all abilities with an abundance of slides and swings, climbing areas, explore zones and ample seating for parents. Kids will also find spinners, seesaws, a dedicated toddler area, and a unique blend of nature, adventure, and sensory play zones featuring rope climbing, water play, and musical instruments.
And the best part for us adults? A great little cafe has just opened up serving quality coffee and snacks.

Whilst this park is a genuine 10/10 there are two common gripes which you should be aware of. Firstly, there’s little to no shade - an unusual oversight in playground planning in Sydney. Secondly, there is an accessibly entry gate that provides gate latches below adult waist level which we saw two year olds managing to open before attempting great escapes (this happens a lot). These aren’t deal breakers but worth knowing in advance.
You can find the playground off Paul St, Bondi Junction.

blocks.text: Bondi, a world-renowned beachside suburb in Sydney, Australia, is not just a haven for sun-seekers and surfers; it’s a vibrant community full of activities and experiences that visitors can enjoy. As summer unfolds, the shimmering sands and sparkling waters of Bondi Beach become the epicentre of a myriad of activities, perfect for those looking to make the most out of the sunny season.
Morning Yoga Sessions on Bondi Beach

Kick-start your summer mornings with a serene yoga session on the shores of Bondi Beach. The combination of gentle waves and the soft morning sunlight creates an unmatched ambiance for practicing yoga. Local studios often offer sunrise classes, including at Icebergs, catering to all levels. It’s a perfect way to rejuvenate your body and mind while enjoying the natural beauty of Bondi.
Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk

The Bondi to Coogee walk is an iconic activity that truly comes to life in summer. This 6km trail offers breathtaking views of the coastline, passing through beaches, parks, and cliffs. It’s an excellent way for locals to stay active while enjoying some of the best views that Sydney has to offer. Don’t forget to pack water, sunscreen, and your camera to capture the stunning scenery.
Surfing Lessons and Sessions

Bondi is synonymous with surfing, and summer is the perfect time to ride the waves. Whether you’re a beginner eager to learn or an experienced surfer looking to hone your skills, numerous local surf schools offer lessons tailored to all levels. There’s nothing quite like the thrill of catching a wave at Bondi Beach.
Explore the Bondi Markets

The Bondi Markets, held every weekend at the Bondi Beach Public School, are a treasure trove of unique finds. From vintage clothing and handmade jewelry to gourmet food and local artwork, there’s something for everyone. It’s a great way to support local artisans and find something special.
Bondi’s Vibrant Food Scene

Bondi’s culinary scene is as diverse as its population. Summer is the perfect time to explore the suburb’s cafes, restaurants, and bars. Whether it’s enjoying fresh seafood, sipping on craft cocktails, or trying out vegan delicacies, Bondi’s food scene is sure to tantalize your taste buds.
Outdoor Cinemas

Enjoy a movie under the stars at one of Bondi’s outdoor cinemas. These pop-up venues offer a unique viewing experience, showing a mix of classic and contemporary films. Bring a blanket, grab some popcorn, and relax under the summer night sky.
Bondi Icebergs Club

No Bondi summer is complete without a visit to the iconic Bondi Icebergs Club. With its famous ocean pool and sauna, it’s the perfect place to cool off and unwind. The club also offers a fantastic dining experience with panoramic views of Bondi Beach.

Bondi in summer is more than just a beach; it’s a vibrant community bursting with activities. From yoga at dawn to outdoor movies at dusk, there’s something for every local to enjoy. Embrace the Bondi lifestyle this summer and immerse yourself in all the experiences this stunning suburb has to offer.

blocks.text: After two decades of hosting one of the most iconic New Year’s Day parties in Sydney, Icebergs Dining Room and Bar at Bondi Beach is changing its tradition. For 20 years, this exclusive event, orchestrated by Maurice Terzini, has been a highlight of the social calendar, attracting a glamorous crowd, including international celebrities and local luminaries. Notable attendees over the years have included Hollywood actors Matt Damon, Chris Hemsworth, and Adrien Brody, Victoria’s Secret model Erin Heatherton, and prominent Sydney figure John Ibrahim. This illustrious event was synonymous with the start of the new year, combining breathtaking views of Bondi Beach with high-profile entertainment and an electrifying atmosphere. However, this January 1st will mark a departure from this long-standing tradition. Instead of the famed high-energy bash, Icebergs is opting for a more subdued, elegant affair, focusing on sit-down meals that offer a different kind of celebration while maintaining the venue’s renowned sophistication and style.

North Bondi Fish is celebrating New Year’s Day 2024 with a vibrant day party. Starting at 12 pm, the event will feature DJs on deck, playing fresh music throughout the day. Guests can enjoy icy cocktails and a shared set menu specializing in seafood. Tickets are priced at $120, which includes access to the seafood spread. A separate children’s menu is available for $25 per person. The party promises a lively atmosphere, making it a great way to kick off the new year at one of Bondi’s popular venues.

This year, guests are invited to join either a classic lunch or a sunset lunch, both offering stunning views of Bondi Beach atop the Pacific Ocean at Icebergs . The classic lunch is scheduled from 12 pm to 3 pm, while the sunset lunch will take place from 4 pm to 10 pm.

At Promenade , celebrate the arrival of 2024 with an exclusive beach-side lunch. Offering a luxurious four-course set menu for $169, the culinary experience includes caviar on potato scallops, a signature seafood platter, Westholme Wagyu, barbecued snapper with side dishes, and a dulce de leche pavlova for dessert. Enhance the experience with an optional 2.5-hour all-inclusive Champagne package. Set against the backdrop of endless ocean views, the event features beats by DJ Murray Lake, ensuring a lively and memorable start to the new year. Book now for a sophisticated and festive celebration at one of the most sought-after beach locations.
At Glory Days , your New Year’s Day celebration ticket includes two hours of canapés paired with premium drinks from 1pm to 3pm, offering a stylish and enjoyable way to ring in 2024.

For those seeking a recovery or celebratory brunch on New Year’s Day, Rocker presents a special one-off bottomless experience. Priced at $99 per person, this event includes 1.5 hours of drinks accompanied by delectable sharing-style dishes. For those desiring an extra boost, special upgrades are available to enhance the experience. This event promises a delightful way to either recover from or continue the New Year’s celebrations.
Check with venues directly for bookings/ticket availability.

blocks.text: New Year’s Eve in Sydney is a truly memorable experience. Typically balmy weather, unmatched fireworks around the harbour and a jovial atmosphere make this a must-do on the Australian events calendar.

For those based in and around Bondi we’ve put together a list of places you may want to check out. Whilst Bondi itself has some great parties it isn’t the main attraction in Sydney for New Year’s Eve as you can’t view the harbour fireworks in Bondi. That said, Bondi does do New Year’s Day well (see our guide to NYD here )

To discover the best New Year’s Eve vantage points near Bondi in Sydney’s eastern suburbs, it’s essential to consider a variety of factors like the view of the fireworks, accessibility, and crowd management. Here’s an overview of what you can expect:
Bondi Beach:

Famous for its stunning views and vibrant atmosphere, Bondi Beach offers a unique seaside experience for New Year’s Eve celebrations. Although not a spot for watching the Harbour fireworks, it’s perfect for those who prefer a beach setting with a festive atmosphere or for those who are keen to set themselves up at a bar and spend the night there.
Dover Heights:

Offering elevated views of Sydney Harbour, Dover Heights is an excellent choice for those who want to enjoy the fireworks from a distance. The area’s high vantage points provide a panoramic view of the city, making it a less crowded alternative to the central locations. Dudley Page Reserve is the number one spot here and is perfect for families with a capacity of 3000. It’s BYO food but alcohol must be purchased onsite. Given the family friendly nature of the event this is not the place to go if you plan on getting drunk and rowdy as it won’t be tolerated by authorities. Tickets must be reserved in advance and you can find more information here .
Vaucluse:

Strickland Estate in Vaucluse is another ticketed event that provides some of the best panoramic views of the Harbour Bridge fireworks. Alcohol and food is for sale and food only is BYO. Tickets must be reserved in advance and you can find more information here .

Known for its picturesque setting, Nielsen Park offers a serene environment to ring in the New Year. It’s a fantastic spot for families, offering clear views of the Harbour Bridge and Opera House, albeit from a distance.
A lesser-known spot, Parsley Bay Reserve is perfect for a peaceful evening. While the views of the main fireworks are limited, the setting is ideal for a relaxed celebration
Rose Bay:

Dumaresq Reserve is a great vantage point that does not require a ticket but does have limited capacity meaning you should be setting up camp as soon as it opens at 3pm. No food or alcohol can be bought here and alcohol is prohibited. Rose Bay foreshore is another option with access from 3pm. The views of the bridge are limited but for a low key evening this could be a good option.
Double Bay:

Murray Rose Pool & Blackburn Gardens is an official vantage point that caters to 1000 people. Tickets aren’t required and the site opens at 3pm. There are limited views of the fireworks here but the atmosphere is always great.
Coogee Beach:

Similar to Bondi, Coogee Beach offers a more relaxed and spacious environment. While the view of the Harbour fireworks don’t exist, the beach often hosts its own festivities, including local fireworks, making it a great family-friendly option.
Point Piper:

Duff Reserve is a free vantage point that opens at midday with a capacity of 100 people. It has limited views of the fireworks but given the small crowd is a nice way to welcome the new year with friends. Note that there are no food or drink facilities here and alcohol is prohibited.
Bronte Beach:

Bronte, nestled between Bondi and Coogee, is a quieter spot but in recent years has been a magnet for partygoers that have attracted national and international headlines as a result of the mess left behind. Council has claimed it is cracking down on this location and it’s yet to be seen what impact this will have. Our advice is to steer clear as you won’t see the fireworks from here.
Watsons Bay:

Situated at the tip of the South Head peninsula, Watsons Bay offers spectacular views of the Harbour albeit from a distance. The area is known for its tranquil setting and is a great place to enjoy both the 9 PM family fireworks and the midnight display.
Darling Point:

McKell Park is a hidden gem that is a little more secluded, offering stunning views of the Harbour Bridge. It’s a fantastic spot for a quieter, more intimate New Year’s Eve experience. The site opens at midday and tickets aren’t required.

Yaranabee Park which adjoins Rushcutters Park offers a good balance between decent views and a less crowded environment. It’s a fantastic option for those who want to enjoy a view of the fireworks with a little extra space. The further you walk along the footpath towards the main body of the harbour the better your view will be.

Each of these locations has its unique charm and offers a different experience for New Year’s Eve celebrations. Whether you prefer a beach party, a quiet picnic, or a panoramic view of the fireworks, Sydney’s eastern suburbs have something for everyone. Remember to check for any local restrictions or ticketing requirements, as some spots might be regulated on New Year’s Eve.

title: Bondi Beach Etiquette: The Local Rules
metaDescription: The unwritten rules of Bondi Beach - swimming between the flags, sharing the sand, surf etiquette and how not to stand out as a tourist.

blocks.text: It’s summer which means it’s time for a reminder on Bondi Beach etiquette. Whilst it comes down to simple respect, unfortunately these simple rules are ignored far too frequently.
Leave your music at home. There’s nowhere on the beach where your music won’t be overheard and whilst you may love the sound of your own Spotify playlist there’s a pretty high chance others won’t.

Swim between the flags. This could not be more obvious but it’s consistently ignored, often by those who need to follow this. It’s simple, swim here to avoid drowning. Here’s more information if you need it.

Don’t fall victim to the backpacker bake. We’ve all seen it, the day one backpacker at Bondi who convinces themselves that they don’t need sunscreen because they never got burnt lying on the Common in London. Lobster red skin is wrong on every level so do what everyone else does and be sun smart.

Park responsibly. We get it. After half an hour of looking for a carpark the threat of a parking ticket starts to look like a risk worth talking. But don’t park across driveways or in a No Parking zone that blocks someone else’s ability to enter or exit their parking space. You wouldn’t believe how often this happens in summer but be warned, you will get that $400 ticket along with a call from the police if you block a driveway. It’s not worth it. Check out our parking guide here - it may help.

No booze. Don’t bring alcohol to the beach and stay away if you’re blind drunk and can’t control yourself. The beach is busy and for everyone - don’t ruin other people’s day by acting like a dick head.

Respect the lifeguards. They are there to protect everyone on the beach and should be treated with respect. Follow their instructions, swim between the flags, surf away from the flags and if you want a chat and they are busy don’t take it personally - they have a job to do. Interested in knowing more about the lifeguards? Click here .

Save yourself from beach rage by choosing your position on the beach carefully. If you want some personal space don’t sit at the far end of North Bondi or between the flags. This area is popular and space is in short supply and you will have families sit right next to you which they have every right to do. If you’d like some space, the middle of the beach or south Bondi is your best bet.

Don’t hover in the Queen Elizabeth Pde beach carpark . On a busy day you’d rather be anywhere else than trying to find a park at the beach. So please don’t make it worse by stopping near the entrance waiting for cars between you and the vehicle in front to leave their spot. It creates gridlock on Campbell Pde and is just a really average thing to do.

Check your pram before leaving North Bondi . There’s normally more than 30 black prams lined up at North Bondi, many the same make and model. You’d be surprised how often the wrong pram is taken which, if you have kids you know can cause chaos when a toddler discovers their favourite pram toy is nowhere to be found.
No foil surfing . You’re going to decapitate someone at such a busy beach so leave it at home.

Don’t do anything that overtly draws attention to yourself . This is broad but is a pretty solid rule. Despite what you may think of yourself people aren’t at the beach to see you. Sure, show off your chiselled body but leave the peacocking away and just try to have fun.

Set your tent up from midway to the back of the beach so you don’t obstruct everyone’s view of the water. That said, if someone does set up a tent in front of you, that’s okay. It’s the beach. It’s public. You’ll be okay.
Don’t smoke. Don’t vape.
No jeans. Unless it’s winter there’s no reason to wear jeans at the beach. Everyone will take pity on you for being so miserable and it will just bring the mood down.
Take your rubbish with you when you leave. There are bins everywhere so you won’t need to walk further than a couple of hundred metres to get rid of it. This one is a no brainer.
Be mindful of the kids. There are little kids everywhere so be considerate when you’re in and around the water.
When bodysurfing be mindful of those in front of you and position yourself, as best you can, to not immediately crash right into someone.

Be considerate, and not a creep, when taking photos. Everyone loves to capture a shot of their day out at Bondi but leave the long lenses behind and just take a couple of quick snaps in the general beach direction before moving on. There’s nothing worse than seeing someone with their professional camera standing in one spot taking pictures of people in the beach. Even worse when they are in jeans (see rule #13).
Finally, we’d love the millions of photos taken each year for Instagram to be tagged @visitbondibeach and #visitbondibeach.

blocks.text: Exploring Bondi Beach with kids is a delight, with a range of activities that cater to young adventurers and their parents. Here’s a family-friendly guide to making the most of this iconic Sydney destination:

1. Bondi Beach Playground: With its boat-themed equipment and stunning sea views, this enclosed playground offers a safe space for children to play and parents to relax. BBQ and picnic areas are available, making it perfect for a family day out .

2. North Bondi Children’s Pool: This shallow wading pool is ideal for little ones to splash around in. Located at the northern end of the beach, it’s a great spot for families to spend a few hours. Don’t forget the buckets and spades for beachside fun .

3. Surfing Lessons: Bondi Beach is a great place for the whole family to learn to surf, with lessons available for children aged five and up. Family group lessons provide a memorable experience for everyone .

4. Icebergs Pool: The famous Bondi Icebergs Pool is a must-visit, featuring a smaller pool alongside the 50m lap pool, where families can swim and enjoy the sun. Remember to apply sunscreen and maybe avoid the middle of the day when the sun is strongest .

5. Family Walks: Take a leisurely stroll along the Bondi Beach Promenade or embark on the Bondi to Coogee Coastal Path for stunning views and fresh ocean air. These walks are suitable for strollers and offer sights like the Bondi Graffiti Wall and skate park for older kids .

6. Kid-Friendly Dining: Bondi Beach has several family-friendly cafes and restaurants. From the modern Australian cuisine of Bills Bondi Beach to the fresh, organic offerings of Cali Press, there’s something to satisfy any palate. Heart Cafe is not only great for a meal but also supports a social cause .

Whether you’re planning to catch the first light on the beach, teach the kids to ride their first wave, or enjoy a tasty meal after a day of exploration, Bondi Beach offers an abundance of family-friendly activities that are sure to create lasting memories.

blocks.text: Bronte Beach, Sydney’s coastal gem, attracts swimmers, surfers, and picnickers year-round. While it offers a slice of paradise, finding parking can be a bit like searching for treasure - challenging but rewarding when successful. Here’s your essential guide to parking at Bronte Beach, so you can spend less time circling for spots and more time enjoying the sun, sea, and sand.
Council Car Parks: The Go-To Options

The Bronte Beach area has council-operated car parks that are convenient and closest to the beach. These car parks are usually pay-and-display, with rates depending on the season. The Bronte Cutting Car Park, located right by the beach, is the most popular. Early arrival during peak seasons is advised, as spaces fill up quickly.
Street Parking: A Game of Timing

Surrounding residential streets offer metered parking options and unlike Bondi Beach there is a chance of getting a spot within walking distance of the beach if you don’t mind a 5 minute walk. These are a good bet if you're planning a shorter visit and can snag a spot. Be mindful of the parking signs and restrictions, as they vary from street to street and are enforced rigorously. Pacific St and Bronte Rd are your best bets for looking for parking.
For the Early Birds and Late Swimmers
If you’re an early bird or a late swimmer, you’ll find that parking becomes significantly easier. Enjoy a serene morning or a tranquil sunset at Bronte, with the added bonus of hassle-free parking.
Remember, Plan Ahead

A day at Bronte Beach is worth a little pre-planning. Check the council website for the latest updates on parking fees and times before you set off. With this guide in hand, you’re all set for a stress-free visit to one of Sydney’s most beloved beaches.

blocks.text: Bondi Beach is Australia’s most visited beach, with around 2.9 million visitors annually​​.
Icebergs pool is turned into an advertising canvas a few times a year. See every example from the past 15 years here .
A life size buddha once overlooked Bondi Beach as part of an art exhibition.
Bondi Icebergs pool is emptied and cleaned every Thursday.
The beach stretches about 1 km in length and becomes especially crowded during summer​​.
It recorded its highest temperature at 117.14°F (47.3°C) on January 7th, 2018​​.
Known for its vibrant street art, the Bondi Beach Graffiti Wall dates back to the 1980s​​.
Bondi Beach is a popular filming location for TV shows and movies, including 'Bondi Rescue'​​.
The largest surfing lesson was held at Bondi Beach with 320 participants in December 2015​​.
Home to the oldest surf life-saving club in Australia, the Bondi Surf Bathers’ Life Saving Club founded in 1907​​.
The tragic event known as Black Sunday occurred here in February 1938, where around 250 people were swept out to sea​​.
The last recorded fatal shark attack at Bondi Beach was in 1929​​.
Bondi Icebergs is the most photographed swimming pool in the world and offers stunning ocean views​​.
The name "Bondi" originates from the Aboriginal word "Boondi," which means "noise made by sea waves breaking on the beach," akin to the English word "surf"​​.
Bondi Beach was made accessible to the public in 1882 after it had been private land under the "O'Brien Estate"​​.
The area has experienced significant cultural shifts, including becoming home to Jewish migrants post-World War II, which influenced its development into an affluent enclave​​.

Bondi Beach has been a battleground for beach attire decency from as early as 1907, with notable incidents including American actress Jean Parker being escorted off the beach in 1951 due to her skimpy bikini​​.
A hermit named Jhyimy "Two Hats" Mhiyles became a local celebrity during the 2000 Sydney Olympic Games for his lifestyle and poetry recitals to visitors​​.
Bondi Beach has several heritage-listed sites and was added to the Australian National Heritage List in 2008​​.
In 2011, free Wi-Fi was implemented at Bondi Beach for visitors and locals​​.
The beach hosted the beach volleyball competition at the 2000 Summer Olympics, with the construction of a temporary 10,000-seat stadium and additional courts for the event​​.
The first-aid kits used by the lifeguards on "Bondi Rescue" have evolved to include advanced medical equipment that one would typically expect to find in hospitals​​.
Hastings Pde in North Bondi is one of Australia’s most exclusive, and expensive streets.
During peak season, the lifeguards perform between 30 to 50 rescues each day.
Lifeguards perform night patrols sometimes, especially during special events like New Year’s Eve.
Before it was named "Bondi Rescue," other names considered for the TV show included “Life on the Beach” and “Guardians of Bondi”
Bondi Icebergs is recognized as the most photographed pool in the world​​.
To become an official member of the Bondi Icebergs, swimmers must swim there 3 out of 4 Sundays each month during winter for five years.

blocks.text: If you're seeking a hidden gem along the picturesque coast of New South Wales, Australia, the Bronte Ocean Pool is a must-visit destination. Nestled within the breathtaking Bronte Beach, this tranquil ocean pool offers a refreshing escape from the hustle and bustle of city life. In this insider's guide, we'll cover everything you need to know about the Bronte Ocean Pool, from its location and accessibility to opening hours and costs.
Location: Where is the Bronte Ocean Pool?

The Bronte Ocean Pool is located in the eastern suburbs of Sydney, Australia. Specifically, it's situated at Bronte Beach, which is part of the famous Eastern Beaches coastal strip. Bronte Beach is flanked by the equally stunning Bondi Beach to the north and Coogee Beach to the south, making it an ideal destination for beach enthusiasts.

This ocean pool is nestled between the rugged cliffs of Bronte, providing a unique swimming experience that combines the natural beauty of the coastline with the comfort and safety of a man-made pool. The pool itself is carved into the rocks and blends seamlessly with the surrounding environment.
Getting There: How to Access Bronte Ocean Pool
Getting to Bronte Beach and the ocean pool is relatively straightforward, whether you're traveling from within Sydney or from farther afield. Here are some transportation options:

By Car: If you have access to a car, you can easily reach Bronte Beach by driving along Bronte Road, where there's ample parking available nearby. However, parking can be limited during peak times, so arriving early is advisable.

Public Transport: Sydney's efficient public transport system provides several options. You can take a train to Bondi Junction and then catch a bus that will drop you off near Bronte Beach. Buses are a convenient and eco-friendly way to reach the area.

Walking: For those who enjoy a scenic walk, the Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk is a popular route that passes through Bronte Beach and the ocean pool. This coastal walk offers stunning ocean views and takes approximately 1-2 hours, depending on your pace.
Cycling: If you prefer cycling, you can easily ride to Bronte Beach. There are bike racks available for securing your bicycle.
Accessibility: Can Anyone Swim At The Bronte Ocean Pool?

One of the fantastic aspects of the Bronte Ocean Pool is that it's open to the public, and anyone can access it. Whether you're a local resident looking for a peaceful morning swim or a visitor exploring Sydney's coastline, you're welcome to enjoy the pool's serene waters.

The pool is designed to be inclusive and safe for swimmers of all skill levels. Lifeguards are typically on duty during daylight hours, providing an extra layer of safety for those enjoying the pool. Families, solo travelers, and couples alike can relish in the beauty and tranquility of this coastal oasis.
Cost: Is It Free?

Good news for budget-conscious travelers: access to the Bronte Ocean Pool is absolutely free! There are no entrance fees or charges for swimming in this natural saltwater pool. This makes it an affordable option for anyone seeking a refreshing dip in the ocean without breaking the bank.

However, if you plan to use the nearby showers and changing facilities, keep in mind that these may require a small fee, usually coin-operated. It's a small price to pay for the convenience of freshening up after your swim.
Opening Hours: When Is It Open?

The Bronte Ocean Pool is typically open year-round, allowing visitors to enjoy its serene waters throughout the seasons. However, the pool's accessibility may vary slightly depending on the time of year and weather conditions.
During the warmer months, from October to April, the pool is generally open from sunrise to sunset. This provides ample daylight hours for swimming and sunbathing on the surrounding rocks.

In the cooler months, from May to September, the pool's opening hours may be slightly reduced, and it's advisable to check the latest information regarding lifeguard hours and pool accessibility. Despite the cooler weather, Bronte's natural beauty still shines, and the ocean pool remains a peaceful retreat.
To Summarise…

The Bronte Ocean Pool is a hidden gem along the stunning coastline of Sydney's Eastern Beaches. Accessible to all and free of charge, it offers a serene and safe swimming experience that combines the best of the natural ocean and a man-made pool. Whether you're a local looking for a refreshing escape or a traveler seeking a unique coastal experience, Bronte Beach and its ocean pool are a must-visit destination. So, pack your swimsuit, hop on public transport, and discover the beauty of the Bronte Ocean Pool for yourself.

The club also takes part in community events, and many members form connections that extend beyond the morning runs. For visitors, this provides an authentic experience of the local Sydney culture and an opportunity to receive recommendations for enjoying the city from residents.

In essence, the 440 Run Club at Bronte Beach is a straightforward, welcoming option for maintaining fitness while visiting Sydney. It provides an excellent opportunity for both exercise and socialising, all set against the backdrop of Bronte Beach’s beautiful coastal environment.

blocks.text: When you think of Bondi Beach, the first images that probably come to mind are sun, surf, and sand. But what if you find yourself at Bondi Beach on a rainy day? Don’t worry; there are still plenty of things to do and enjoy even when the weather isn’t cooperating.

The Bondi Pavilion is a cultural hub that hosts art exhibitions, live performances, and workshops. Check their schedule to see if there are any events or exhibitions that interest you. It’s an excellent opportunity to appreciate local art and culture while staying dry.

Gould Street, just a short walk from the beach, is home to numerous boutique stores, surf shops, and fashion retailers. Spend some time exploring the shops and picking up unique souvenirs or stylish clothing to remember your Bondi visit.

Bondi Beach is known for its vibrant street art scene, and one of the best places to see it is the Bondi Beach Graffiti Wall. This ever-changing canvas showcases the work of local and international artists. Grab your umbrella and take a stroll to admire the colourful and creative artwork.
Take a Coastal Walk:

While it might not be ideal for sunbathing, a rainy day can create a different kind of beauty along Bondi’s famous coastal walk. The dramatic waves and moody skies can add an extra layer of beauty to the stunning coastal scenery. Just bring a raincoat!
Relax at Bondi’s Day Spas:

Attend a Yoga or Fitness Class:

The ultimate wet weather activity. Just up the road from Bondi Beach you can visit Westfield’s cinemas and spend a few hours away from the inclement weather.

One of the iconic landmarks at Bondi Beach is the Bondi Icebergs Club and its famous pool. Whilst it’s not the first thing that would spring to mind, even on a rainy day you can take a dip in the saltwater pool while enjoying breathtaking views of the ocean. It’s a unique experience that you won’t want to miss.

So, while a rainy day at Bondi Beach may not be what you initially envisioned, it can still be a memorable and enjoyable experience. From indulging in spa treatments or simply sipping a hot coffee at a cozy cafe, there are plenty of ways to make the most of your time at Bondi, even when the weather is less than perfect. blocks.text: Bondi Beach is nestled along the eastern coastline of Sydney, Australia. It’s part of the greater Sydney metropolitan area and is renowned for its beauty and popularity as a surf destination. Bondi’s location, like many coastal areas, means it’s a hub for marine life, including various species of sharks. However, before you get worried, it’s crucial to understand the dynamics of shark encounters at Bondi.
Sharks in the Area

Bondi Beach, like most Australian coastal regions, is home to various shark species. The most common types in the area include the Port Jackson shark, wobbegongs, and occasionally, bronze whalers. These sharks are typically not considered dangerous to humans and are rarely responsible for shark incidents.
Shark Incidents at Bondi

While Bondi Beach is known for its shark sightings, it’s important to note that the vast majority of these encounters are harmless. Bondi has a sophisticated shark detection and monitoring system in place to ensure the safety of swimmers and surfers. Lifeguards regularly patrol the waters, and shark alarms are sounded if a potentially dangerous species is spotted.
Bondi’s Safety Measures
Bondi Beach is serious about safety, and they’ve invested heavily in various strategies to minimize the risk of shark incidents. The measures include:
1. Shark Nets: Bondi Beach employs shark nets that run parallel to the shore. These nets serve as a physical barrier, reducing the chances of dangerous sharks entering the swimming area.
2. Surveillance and Monitoring: Lifeguards are vigilant in watching for shark activity. They use binoculars and drones to spot sharks and assess their potential threat to beachgoers.
3. Education and Awareness: Signs and information boards are placed around the beach, educating visitors about shark safety and what to do in case of a shark sighting.
4. Emergency Protocols: Bondi Beach has well-defined emergency protocols in case of a shark incident. Lifeguards are trained to react swiftly to protect beachgoers.
Real Shark Encounters

It’s important to acknowledge that while shark incidents are rare at Bondi Beach, they do occasionally happen. However, these incidents typically involve minor interactions or non-dangerous species. Bondi’s proactive approach to safety has ensured that these encounters result in minimal harm.
What to Do in Case of a Shark Sighting

If you ever find yourself at Bondi Beach and witness a shark sighting, it’s essential to remain calm and follow the advice of lifeguards. The lifeguards are highly trained to handle such situations. Typically, they will sound the shark alarm, and beachgoers will be advised to exit the water promptly. It’s crucial to heed these warnings and stay out of the water until the all-clear signal is given.
Enjoying Bondi Beach Safely
Bondi Beach is a remarkable destination that offers sun, surf, and relaxation. To make the most of your visit while ensuring safety, consider these tips:
1. Swim Between the Flags: Bondi’s lifeguards mark safe swimming areas with red and yellow flags. Always swim between these flags to stay within the monitored zone.
2. Respect Wildlife: Remember that you’re sharing the ocean with various marine creatures. Be respectful of their habitat, and don’t disturb or harass any wildlife you encounter.
3. Stay Informed: Keep an eye on beach safety signs and listen to lifeguards’ instructions. Being informed can help you make safe decisions while at the beach.

So, does Bondi Beach have sharks? Yes, it does, but the presence of sharks should not deter you from experiencing the beauty and excitement of this iconic Australian destination. Bondi’s proactive safety measures and vigilant lifeguards mean that compared to most beaches Bondi is one of the safest when it comes to shark activity.

blocks.text: Come October in Sydney, it’s that time of year when Daylight Saving Time kicks in. This simple guide will help you navigate the transition smoothly.
When Does It Start?

Daylight Saving Time in Sydney typically starts on the first Sunday in October. In 2023, that’s October 1st. Remember to set your clocks forward by one hour at 2:00 AM local standard time, so it becomes 3:00 AM local daylight time.
Why Daylight Saving?

The idea behind it is to make better use of natural daylight during the longer days of summer. This means more daylight in the evenings, making it perfect for outdoor activities, sports, and enjoying Sydney’s beautiful landscapes.
What to Do?
1. Adjust Your Clocks: Ensure all your clocks, including those in your home, car, and electronic devices, are set one hour forward.
2. Check Alarm Settings: Don’t forget to adjust your alarms, especially if you have an early morning routine.
3. Enjoy Longer Evenings: Take advantage of the extended daylight hours to explore Sydney’s beaches, parks, and outdoor attractions.
4. Plan Accordingly: Keep in mind that public transportation schedules may change, so check with relevant authorities for updated timetables.
5. Safety First: With more outdoor activities, remember to stay safe, stay hydrated, and use sunscreen to protect your skin from the stronger sun.
6. Spring Cleaning: Some people use the DST change as a reminder to perform routine tasks like checking smoke detectors and changing air filters.

Daylight Saving Time in Sydney brings a refreshing change to your daily routine down at Bondi, offering more opportunities to enjoy outdoor activities. So, make sure you’re ready to spring forward and make the most of those longer evenings!

blocks.text: Sculpture by the Sea is making its return to the iconic Bondi to Tamarama Beach coastal walk for 2023, offering a one-of-a-kind, free-to-the-public exhibition. It's a sensational event that combines natural beauty with creative expression, making it a must-see for anyone in Sydney during this period. Here's a practical guide to making the most out of your visit.
When It’s On:
20th October - 6th November, 2023
Where it Begins: Bondi Beach

The exhibition kicks off at Bondi Beach, a world-renowned destination celebrated for its golden sands and surfing culture. To get there, you can take a bus from Bondi Junction or simply catch an Uber. Once you arrive, you'll see the starting signs and artworks near the beach. From there, the 2km long coastal walk towards Tamarama Beach is adorned with sculptures that beg to be pondered and photographed.
Duration: A Three-Week Spectacular

The Sculpture by the Sea exhibition lasts for three weeks, ample time for both locals and tourists to plan a visit. Over this period, more than 100 sculptures by artists from Australia and across the globe will be on display.
Best Time to Experience it

Weekdays are generally quieter than weekends, especially during mornings or late afternoons. This is crucial if you’re planning to take photos without throngs of people photobombing your shots. If you're an early bird, a sunrise stroll offers quieter moments and ethereal lighting-ideal for both photography and solitary contemplation.
Be Mindful of the Foot Traffic

The path can get incredibly crowded, especially during weekends or public holidays. While the festive atmosphere adds to the event's charm, it might not be everyone's cup of tea. Remember to be mindful of other spectators and keep a safe distance from the artworks; they're meant for public enjoyment, but they're also priceless pieces of art.
Amenities: Public Bathrooms and Restaurants

Public bathrooms are available at both Bondi and Tamarama beaches, but options are limited along the coastal walk itself. Therefore, it's wise to take a bathroom break before you embark on the journey.

As for food and drink, Bondi has an extensive range of cafes and restaurants to choose from. However, there are fewer options at Tamarama, which is more residential. You might want to pack some snacks and water for the walk.
A Brief History of Famous Sculptures
Over the years, Sculpture by the Sea has displayed several awe-inspiring pieces that have captured public imagination:
"House of Mirrors" by NEON: This mirrored structure played with perspectives and had people gazing at distorted reflections of themselves and the ocean.
"Horizon" by Lucy Humphrey: A giant, water-filled acrylic sphere, it transformed its surroundings into a shifting, dream-like landscape.
"The Bottles" by Simon McGrath: This sculpture featured a series of oversized milk bottles that begged the question of environmental sustainability.
"Walking" by Sean Henry: This sculpture showed a man walking against the wind, a piece that invoked the struggle and perseverance in human life.

Sculpture by the Sea in 2023 promises to be an extraordinary blend of art and nature. So grab your hat, sunscreen, and camera, and make your way to Bondi to immerse yourself in this captivating experience. It’s a walk you won't forget anytime soon!
Remember, the exhibition is free, but donations are welcomed to support this extraordinary community event. Enjoy your artistic odyssey along one of Australia’s most famous coastal walks!

metaDescription: The Sunday drummers on North Bondi's grassy knoll - the story of Bondi Sunset Music and the beach's best free Sunday session.
h1: The Drummers On The North Bondi Grassy Knoll
intro: The Drummers On The North Bondi Grassy Knoll — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach The Drummers On The North Bondi Grassy Knoll Seemingly out of nowhere one day on North Bondi’s grassy knoll, a collective of drummers known as Bondi Sunset Music appeared, reshaping Sunday afternoons at the beach. Their mission?

blocks.text: Seemingly out of nowhere one day on North Bondi’s grassy knoll, a collective of drummers known as Bondi Sunset Music appeared, reshaping Sunday afternoons at the beach. Their mission? Connecting people through music, dance, and the magic of a beach sunset. We interviewed the group to find out what it’s all about.
When and how did Bondi Sunset Music start?

Bondi sunset music started purely organically when a local musician and musical hobbyist Paulo Dos Santos Charles Myssy bumped into each other on the grassy knoll one afternoon as the sun was setting, they were both playing their own instruments solo, until they decided to connect and play together, from that day, Paulo invited Charles to join him and his son Alex Dos Santos who at the time was only 9 years old to play on one Sunday afternoon. Since then, they played every Sunday and more people began to join. People like Hector Martinez and Renato Jelen other bondi locals. It has since grown to a large community where people can come together and join in.
Where and when can people find you?

People can find us playing every Sunday, depending on the weather at bondi beach from 3pm all the way til Sunset. We’ve been mixing up the locations recently, usually we play on the grassy knoll, but at the moment we are playing on the beach between ramps 6-7.
What’s the philosophy of the group?

The philosophy of the group is that we want people to re-connect with themselves and each other through dance and music. Nature, bare feet in the earth, live ecstatic tribal drumming, dancing like nobody’s watching, sober drug and alcohol free environment, for the whole community no matter your age or ethnicity, it’s powerful! You don’t have to look far to see the smiles, and the evidence backs it up. Drum circles have been around for hundreds of thousands of years, and for good reason, it’s an incredible ceremony to connect people with themselves, their bodies and others. Loads of studies are out on the positive impact on drum circles for depression and anxiety, and that’s why it blew up especially during covid, people needed a safe space to let loose the stress and worries, and connect during a lonely time.
Who can get involved and how?

We have our main members of the group, but anybody can get involved. We welcome everyone to come and join us for the weekly celebration. We have a structure with how we run the sets, it’s very simple, to ensure everyone stays in rhythm, bring your instruments and join us! We get the kids to play some instruments that we bring and to hang out drums in between. Preparing the next generation of bondi sunset drummers!
You’ve changed the fabric of Bondi on Sunday afternoons, bringing a party vibe to the beach. How has the local community responded?

We’ve had a lot of mostly beautiful support from the locals which we are super grateful for! Without them we wouldn’t have been able to continue this epic event. But like anything, we get mixed feelings. Initially people thought we were bringing trouble, drugs and alcohol to the beach, but we quickly squashed that perception, next we had noise complaints, but through mutual understanding, we’ve kept the sets within limits, only play for a few hours and have regular breaks in between to break it up, and also, had a-lot of negativity during covid because people thought we were spreading the virus. Ultimately we‘ve had our challenges, like any community like any family. But we know our intentions are good and we know the positive impact we have, so many people have formed friendships, relationships from this community and people we’re literally saying to us that without the drums, they probably wouldn’t be here, as it’s given them something to look forward to every week.
Any big plans coming up you can share?
Nothing too crazy or big, I think we are just keeping it simple for now and playing for the community, but eventually we’d like to organise some actual events with some extra entertainment!
Anything else to add?
Just want to thank everyone for the love and support and we hope to see you in Bondi on a Sunday celebrating the sunset with us!

blocks.text: For those seeking a picturesque adventure along the stunning coastline of Sydney, the Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk is an absolute must. This iconic trek offers breathtaking vistas, natural beauty, and a chance to soak in the sun-drenched charm of Australia’s coastal landscape. Whether you’re a seasoned hiker or simply looking for a leisurely stroll, this journey has something for everyone. So, lace up your walking shoes, grab your camera, and let’s embark on this unforgettable journey from Bondi Beach to Bronte Beach.
The Basics: The Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk

The Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk is a well-trodden path along the eastern coastline of Sydney, Australia. Covering approximately 2.5 kilometers (1.5 miles), this coastal trail meanders along cliffs, sandy beaches, and serene parklands. It’s a perfect blend of nature and culture, offering a glimpse into the vibrant beach culture of Sydney while showcasing its natural wonders.
Getting Started: Bondi Beach

Your journey begins at the world-famous Bondi Beach, a sun-soaked haven for surfers, sunbathers, and beach enthusiasts. Arriving early in the morning is a fantastic idea to avoid the crowds and witness the sunrise, casting its golden glow over the golden sands. Bondi is also home to numerous cafes and breakfast spots, so you can fuel up for your adventure. The walk begins just past the Bondi Icebergs Club with a set of stairs on your left just after you pass the terrace dining area of Icebergs at road level.
Sculptures by the Sea: Marking the Start

As you begin your walk, keep an eye out for the Sculptures by the Sea exhibition if you’re visiting during October or November. This annual event transforms the coastline into an open-air art gallery with captivating sculptures by various artists. It’s a unique and artistic start to your journey.
Tamarama Beach: The Hidden Gem

Leaving Bondi behind, the trail takes you to Tamarama Beach, often referred to as “Glamarama” for its fashionable crowd. While it’s smaller and less crowded than Bondi, Tamarama offers stunning ocean views and a glimpse of the iconic Icebergs Club pool, perched above the waves.
Rugged Beauty: Mackenzies Point

The Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk continues its dramatic journey as it passes Mackenzies Point. Here, you’ll find yourself standing atop rugged cliffs, gazing at the vast expanse of the Pacific Ocean. Take a moment to appreciate the raw beauty of the coastline, with waves crashing against the rocks below or, if you’re lucky, the transient beach which only appears every few years ( read more about this phenomenon here ).
Bronte Park: A Lush Oasis

As you approach Bronte Beach, you’ll pass through Bronte Park, a lush green oasis perfect for a picnic or a quick break. It’s a great place to relax and enjoy the shade of towering Norfolk pines. Be sure to explore the park’s layout, as it offers some serene spots hidden away from the main path. There is also a fantastic kids playground in the back corner of the park and a model ride-on train for kids that operates in the warmer months near the ocean pool.
Bronte Beach: A Secluded Gem

Arriving at Bronte Beach feels like stepping into a hidden gem. Smaller and quieter than Bondi, Bronte boasts a tranquil atmosphere that’s perfect for unwinding. The beach is ideal for swimming, sunbathing, or simply watching the waves roll in. Don’t miss the ocean-fed Bronte Baths, a fantastic place for a refreshing swim.
Best Time to Go

The best time to embark on the Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk largely depends on your preferences. If you’re an early riser or a photography enthusiast, consider starting early in the morning to catch the sunrise at Bondi Beach. This not only offers stunning views but also allows you to avoid the crowds that gather later in the day. Alternatively, late afternoons can also be an excellent time to enjoy the walk as the sun casts a warm glow on the coastline.
Key Points of Interest
• Bondi Beach: The starting point, known for its golden sands and vibrant atmosphere.
• Sculptures by the Sea: An art lover’s delight during the annual exhibition.
• Tamarama Beach: A smaller, fashionable beach with ocean views.
• Mackenzies Point: Rugged cliffs and dramatic ocean vistas.
• Bronte Park: A lush green oasis perfect for a picnic or relaxation.
• Bronte Beach: A quieter, secluded beach with a serene ambiance.
• Bronte Baths: Ocean-fed rock pools ideal for swimming.
Walking Tips
• Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection, as much of the path is exposed to the sun.
• Carry water to stay hydrated, especially on hot days.
• The walk is suitable for all fitness levels and is stroller-friendly, but there are some stairs and inclines to navigate.
• Bring your camera or smartphone to capture the stunning views and moments along the way.
• Be mindful of changing weather conditions and check the forecast before heading out.

The Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk is a journey that encapsulates the very essence of Sydney’s coastal beauty. From the iconic Bondi Beach to the tranquil shores of Bronte, this trail offers a sensory experience that combines natural wonders, artistic inspiration, and the laid-back charm of beach culture. Whether you’re a nature enthusiast, an art lover, or simply seeking a peaceful escape, this coastal walk promises a memorable adventure along one of Australia’s most breathtaking coastlines. So, take that first step and discover the beauty that awaits along the Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk.

blocks.text: When we think of Bondi Beach, we envision golden sands, azure waves, and the warm embrace of the Pacific Ocean. However, Mother Nature has her own surprises in store, and one of them is the recently declared El Niño phenomenon. While El Niño is typically associated with extreme weather conditions, including droughts and heatwaves, it may come as a surprise that it can also bring about cooler sea temperatures at Bondi Beach. In this blog post, we’ll explore the science behind this phenomenon and what it means for your next Bondi adventure.
Understanding El Niño

El Niño is a climate phenomenon characterized by the periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. During this event, the normal trade winds that blow east to west across the Pacific weaken or even reverse. This weakening of the trade winds has significant repercussions on weather patterns across the globe.
How El Niño Affects Bondi’s Sea Temperature

1. Changes in Ocean Currents: One of the key ways El Niño influences Bondi’s sea temperature is by altering ocean currents. During El Niño, warm water tends to collect off the coast of South America and throughout the central Pacific instead of spreading eastward. This means that Bondi Beach and the surrounding Australian coastline receive a reduced flow of warm oceanic waters from the Pacific.

2. Colder Waters Off Australia: As warm water accumulates in the central and eastern Pacific, it leads to colder ocean temperatures off the coast of Australia. This cold-water anomaly can persist for several months, directly impacting the sea temperature experienced at Bondi Beach.

3. Reduced Moisture and Rainfall: El Niño also affects the atmospheric conditions over Australia. With the weakening of trade winds, less moisture rises into the atmosphere, leading to lower-than-average rainfall and possible drought conditions. Reduced rainfall can indirectly contribute to cooler sea temperatures, as less freshwater input can lead to a decrease in coastal water temperatures.
Impact on Bondi Beachgoers
For those planning a trip to Bondi during an El Niño event, there are a few noteworthy effects to consider:

1. Cooler Sea: The ocean waters at Bondi Beach may feel cooler than expected during an El Niño event. Swimmers and surfers should be prepared for a refreshing change, but also be cautious of potential changes in currents and wave patterns.

2. Unique Wildlife Sightings: Cooler sea temperatures can attract different marine life to the area. Keep an eye out for unusual species of fish and other creatures that might venture closer to the shore during this time.

3. Drought Conditions: While a dip in sea temperature might be surprising, it’s essential to remember that El Niño often brings drought conditions to the region. This can have wider implications for water supply and local ecosystems, so stay informed about any water restrictions or conservation efforts in place.

El Niño is a complex climate phenomenon that can have a variety of impacts, including cooler sea temperatures at Bondi Beach. While this might be unexpected for beachgoers, it’s just one example of how interconnected the Earth’s climate systems are. So, if you find yourself dipping your toes into slightly cooler waters during an El Niño event, take it as an opportunity to appreciate the wonders of nature and the ever-changing dynamics of our planet. Bondi Beach will always have its charm, regardless of the sea temperature.
