metaDescription: The ultimate guide to the 80km Bondi to Manly walk - the route, how to break it into stages and the best sections to tackle.
h1: Ultimate guide to the 80km Bondi to Manly walk
intro: Ultimate guide to the 80km Bondi to Manly walk — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach Ultimate guide to the 80km Bondi to Manly walk The Bondi to Manly Walk is a spectacular coastal trail stretching approximately 80 kilometers between two of Sydney's most iconic beaches, Bondi Beach and Manly Beach. This stunnin

blocks.text: The Bondi to Manly Walk is a spectacular coastal trail stretching approximately 80 kilometers between two of Sydney's most iconic beaches, Bondi Beach and Manly Beach. This stunning walk offers a unique way to explore Sydney's coastline and its rich cultural and natural heritage, showcasing a diverse range of landscapes from dramatic cliffs to tranquil harborside parks, and offering breathtaking views of the Sydney Harbour, Pacific Ocean, and the city skyline. The walk takes you through some of the city's most picturesque and historically significant suburbs, as well as national parks, harbor foreshores, and pristine beaches.
Key Points Along the Way

Bondi Beach Starting at the world-famous Bondi Beach, the Bondi to Manly Walk kicks off at the southern end, near the Bondi Icebergs Club. As one of Australia's most iconic beaches, Bondi boasts golden sands, a vibrant surf culture, and a bustling promenade lined with trendy cafes, restaurants, and shops. It's the perfect place to begin your coastal adventure.

Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk The walk continues along the rugged coastline, through the Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk. This 2.5-kilometer cliffside trail offers panoramic ocean views, with several lookout points and photo opportunities, including the iconic Bondi Baths and the dramatic cliffs of Mackenzies Point. The path takes you past Tamarama and Bronte beaches, both popular spots for surfing and sunbathing.

Waverley Cemetery Continuing along the coast, you'll pass through the picturesque Waverley Cemetery, a heritage-listed site resting atop the coastal cliffs. The cemetery's serene atmosphere and stunning ocean views make it a unique and memorable part of the walk.

Clovelly Beach Heading further north, the path takes you to the calm waters of Clovelly Beach, a popular spot for swimming and snorkeling. The beach features a narrow bay with a unique rockpool-like swimming area, perfect for families and less experienced swimmers.

Coogee Beach Next, the trail leads you to the bustling Coogee Beach, offering a variety of cafes, restaurants, and shops. Coogee Beach is a popular spot for swimming, surfing, and beach volleyball, as well as a great place to grab a bite to eat or relax in the park.

South Maroubra Beach and Malabar Headland National Park From Coogee Beach, the trail heads south, passing by the rugged cliffs and rock formations of South Maroubra Beach and entering the Malabar Headland National Park. This national park boasts a variety of native flora and fauna and offers fantastic views of the coastline and the city skyline.

La Perouse The walk then heads north to the historic La Perouse area, named after the French explorer who arrived in Botany Bay in 1788. This area features the Bare Island Fort, a military fort built in 1885, and the La Perouse Museum, which showcases the history of the area.

Kamay Botany Bay National Park Continuing north, the trail takes you through the Kamay Botany Bay National Park, home to significant cultural and historical sites, such as Captain Cook's Landing Place and the Meeting Place, where British colonists first encountered the indigenous people of the area.

Kurnell After passing through the national park, you'll arrive in the suburb of Kurnell. Here, you can visit the Captain Cook's Landing Place monument and learn about the history of European settlement in Australia.

Cronulla Beach and Ferry to Bundeena Upon reaching Cronulla Beach, the walk transitions from the easternbeach to the northern side of Sydney. To continue the Bondi to Manly Walk, you'll need to catch a ferry from Cronulla to Bundeena. This scenic ferry ride crosses the waters of Port Hacking and provides fantastic views of the surrounding national parks and waterways. Royal National Park From Bundeena, the trail enters the Royal National Park, Australia's oldest national park, established in 1879. The park is a haven for nature lovers, offering a diverse range of landscapes, from lush rainforests to rugged coastal cliffs. As you traverse the park, be sure to visit the famous Wedding Cake Rock, a unique white rock formation that resembles a tiered wedding cake.

Wattamolla Beach Continuing through the Royal National Park, you'll arrive at the idyllic Wattamolla Beach, a secluded spot with a calm lagoon, perfect for swimming and picnicking. The beach also features a picturesque waterfall and is a popular destination for birdwatching.

Garie Beach and North Era Beach The walk proceeds north, passing the pristine beaches of Garie Beach and North Era Beach, both of which offer secluded spots for swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing in the pristine coastal environment.

Otford Lookout As you leave the Royal National Park and approach Otford Lookout, you'll be treated to panoramic views of the coastline and the Pacific Ocean. The lookout is a perfect spot to rest and take in the surrounding beauty.

Sea Cliff Bridge The trail then takes you along the iconic Sea Cliff Bridge, a 665-meter-long cantilevered bridge that curves around the coastline, offering breathtaking views of the ocean and cliffs.

Wollongong to Sydney Train Upon reaching the northern end of the Sea Cliff Bridge, you'll need to catch a train from the nearby Wollongong suburb of Coalcliff to Sydney's North Shore. This train journey takes you through the picturesque Illawarra Escarpment and along the coastline, providing stunning views of the ocean and surrounding landscape.

Spit Bridge to Manly Walk Once you arrive back in Sydney, the final leg of the Bondi to Manly Walk begins at the Spit Bridge. The Spit Bridge to Manly Walk, also known as the Manly Scenic Walkway, takes you along the harbor foreshore, passing through lush bushland and offering stunning views of Sydney Harbour, the city skyline, and the Northern Beaches.
Dobroyd Head As you make your way along the Manly Scenic Walkway, be sure to stop at Dobroyd Head, a vantage point that offers panoramic views of Sydney Harbour, the city skyline, and the ocean.
Reef Beach and Forty Baskets Beach Continuing along the trail, you'll pass the tranquil waters of Reef Beach and Forty Baskets Beach, both offering secluded spots for swimming and relaxing.

Manly Beach Finally, the Bondi to Manly Walk concludes at the iconic Manly Beach. Known for its surf culture, golden sands, and vibrant atmosphere, Manly Beach is the perfect endpoint for this incredible coastal adventure. Here, you can celebrate the completion of your journey by enjoying a meal or a drink at one of the many cafes, restaurants, and bars lining the beachfront promenade.

blocks.text: Bondi Beach is one of the most iconic and popular beaches in Sydney, Australia. Known for its picturesque views, vibrant atmosphere, and excellent surf, it's no wonder that thousands of locals and tourists flock to Bondi every year. Whether you're a seasoned Bondi-goer or planning your first visit, this locals guide has everything you need to know to make the most of your time at Bondi Beach.
Getting there:

Bondi Beach is located just 7km east of the Sydney CBD, making it easily accessible by public transport. The easiest way to get to Bondi is by taking the 333 or 380 bus from the city. Alternatively, you can catch the train to Bondi Junction and then take the bus or walk to the beach. If you're driving, there is limited parking available at the beach, but it can be difficult to find a spot during peak times.
Things to do:

Surfing: Bondi is a popular spot for surfers of all skill levels. The beach has a wide range of breaks, from beginner-friendly to more challenging. Rent a board and take a lesson from one of the many surf schools on the beach, or bring your own gear and catch a wave on your own.
Swimming: Bondi's famous ocean pool, known as the Bondi Icebergs, is a must-see attraction. The pool is open year-round and offers a safe and protected place to swim, even on the roughest days.
Walking: Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk is a scenic 6km walk that offers breathtaking views of the coast. The walk starts at Bondi and ends at Bronte Beach and takes about 1-2 hours to complete.

Eating and Drinking: Bondi has a wide variety of cafes, restaurants, and bars to choose from. Whether you're looking for a quick bite or a sit-down meal, there's something for everyone. The Bondi Markets, held every Sunday, is a great place to sample some local food and drink.

Fitness: Bondi is a fitness lover's paradise. There are plenty of outdoor gyms and fitness classes, including yoga, Pilates, and boot camp. Join a class or work out on your own with a view of the ocean.
Beach culture:

Bondi Beach has a relaxed and friendly atmosphere, and locals are always happy to welcome visitors. The beach has a strong surf culture, and you'll often see surfers of all ages and skill levels catching waves. The beach is also home to a large number of fitness enthusiasts, and it's not uncommon to see people running, cycling, or doing yoga on the sand.
Safety:

Bondi Beach is generally a safe place to swim, but it's important to be aware of the conditions before entering the water. The beach has both a flagged area and lifeguards on duty to ensure swimmers' safety. However, it's always a good idea to swim between the flags, as the area outside of the flags is not patrolled by lifeguards.
Best time to visit:

Bondi Beach is a great place to visit year-round. However, the best time to visit is during the summer months (December-February) when the weather is warm and the beach is at its busiest. If you're looking for a quieter experience, spring (September-November) or fall (March-May) are good times to visit.

Bondi Beach is a must-visit destination for anyone visiting Sydney. With its beautiful views, vibrant atmosphere, and endless activities, it's no wonder that Bondi is one of the most popular beaches in Australia

blocks.text: There are several ways to get from the Sydney CBD to Bondi Beach, here are a few options:

By Bus: The most convenient way to get to Bondi beach from the city is by bus. The bus route 380 from Circular Quay is the most direct route and it takes around 30 minutes to reach Bondi Junction, from there you can take the bus 333 or 380 and it will take you to Bondi beach.
By Train: You can take the train from the city to Bondi Junction Station, from there you can take the bus 333 or 380 and it will take you to Bondi beach.

By Car: If you prefer to drive, you can take the Eastern Distributor or the Sydney Harbour Tunnel to reach Bondi beach. However, parking can be difficult to find and the beach can get crowded during peak season, so it's best to plan your trip accordingly.
By bike: You can also take a bike tour or rent a bike to reach Bondi beach, this option will give you a chance to enjoy the scenic coastal walk, and also it's a great way to exercise.
It's worth noting that during peak season, traffic and public transport can be busy, so it's best to plan your trip accordingly and allow extra time for your journey.

blocks.text: Visitors from over 100 countries will be pretty familiar with Bondi Beach, having seen plenty of it on TV thanks to 'Bondi Rescue'. The show follows the trials and tribulations of the surf life savers at Bondi Beach who make more than 5,000 rescues a season ( to avoid being on the receiving end see our Bondi swimming guide ). The show has been on since 2006 and gives viewers a good look at what the challenging job involves.

The lifeguards patrol the beach 365 days a year and are employed by the local council (Waverley). The council outlines there role as follows; They put out the flags and rescue equipment, patrol designated public surf bathing and surfcraft areas as well as closely monitor dangerous swimming areas. When necessary they perform rescues and resuscitations. When there are strong rips and a big crowd they may perform over 100 rescues a day. In addition to the front line work they provide information on surf and beach conditions to the public and give beach and water safety talks to schools and community groups.
In addition to the professional lifeguard, dressed in blue, you will see volunteer lifeguards based at the local Surf Life Saving Club in red and yellow.
Lifeguard operation hours:
May to September: 8am- 5pm Late September to start of daylight saving October: 6am- 6pm Late October to end of daylight saving March: 6am- 7pm April: 6am- 6pm

blocks.text: Bondi Beach has a famous reputation as one of the greatest beaches in the world. Everyone who visits talks about how magical the beach is. But, what make Bondi Beach so special.
There are a few reasons why the beach is considered one of the best in the world.

One of the key reasons it is so special is that it is so close to the Sydney CBD – the largest city in Australia. Just 30 minutes in the car from the very heart of the city in good traffic Bondi Beach is an inner city suburb of Sydney.

Bondi Beach has a 1km stretch of sand that extends from the shoreline back at least 100 metres providing an extensive amount of space to cater to tens of thousands of visitors in peak season during summer.

Bondi Beach also boasts the most photographed pool in the world – Bondi Icebergs. Bondi Icebergs pool is a 50m 8 lane pool that is fed directly by seawater. The Bondi Icebers pool is not heated making it a refreshing pool for a swim in the heat of summer and a heart starter in summer. The pool is perched half way into the ocean and waves regularly crash over the wall of the Icebergs pool creating plenty of fun for swimmers.

In addition to a great beach Bondi Beach is famous for its restaurants and bars which are among some of the best in Australia and, indeed, the world. From fine dining to casual beach side cafes Bondi Beach caters for everyone.

The weather in Sydney is temperate all year round and warm for the best part of 8 months of the year which makes this beach particularly appealing. Don’t be fooled though, Bondi is great in winter too with less crowded restaurants and bars and more of a locals feeling.

blocks.text: Bondi Beach is a tourist hotspot year round but when is the best time to visit?

You’d think the obvious answer would be the peak of the Australian summer, from December through to February. There’s no question that summer is a great time to visit Bondi Beach. The weather is warm, the beach is buzzing and the bars are heaving. But summer is not the only time to visit Bondi Beach.

With year round pleasant weather in Sydney spring and autumn are great times to visit where the traffic and parking are more manageable. Autumn in particular is great when the water is still warm from a long hot summer.
For those who may be less interested in swimming winter is also a great time to explore restaurants, markets and shops without the hustle and bustle of the Bondi crowds.

blocks.text: Bondi is one of Australia’s most popular surf beach where surfers can be found in the temperate water year round. Conditions are varied throughout the year but you will find both left and right breaking waves at Bondi.

Learning to surf at Bondi is an easy way to introduce yourself to the sport. Beginner surfers will find calmer conditions at North Bondi, along with a surf school which will supply all equipment and provide a 2 hour surf lesson which will teach you the basics.
Surf lessons are advised particularly if you are not accustomed to spending time in the ocean.
For experienced surfers, look towards middle and south Bondi for the best waves. You will find the best conditions when there are NE or SW winds.
There are surf shops dotted all over Bondi so if you’re looking to buy or rent equipment you will have no problem.

The most important things for any surfer is to stay out of the red and yellow flags which are designated for swimmers only. Stray in between these flags and you will quickly become acquainted with Bondi’s famous lifesavers. The local council has a surfers code at Bondi document which you can check out here .

blocks.text: The Bondi Icebergs Club actually hosts two pools. Along with the main 50-meter lap pool, there is also a smaller pool meant for children and more relaxed swimming. This second pool is shallower and offers a more leisurely experience, making it suitable for families and those looking to enjoy the water without engaging in serious lap swimming.

blocks.text: One of the most common questions from tourists visiting Bondi Beach is where is the nearest train station. There isn't actually a train that takes you directly to Bondi Beach. There is, however, a train that will take you to Bondi Junction which is just 2 kilometres from Bondi Beach.

So, if you are in the CBD or other parts of Sydney serviced by a train and you want to get to Bondi Beach, catch the train to Bondi Junction Station. Then hop on one of the buses to Bondi Beach - they are well sign-posted so you'll have no trouble finding it.

Just be aware that in the peak of summer getting a bus to and from Bondi Beach can be tricky - they are often very full. It might be worth just making the walk downhill to the beach or back up it to return to Bondi Junction. Alternatively, there are Ubers and taxis aplenty at Bondi Beach which you can catch.

blocks.text: The summer ocean swim race season is almost upon us so we've listed the organised ocean swims that start at Bondi Beach. Remember, whist these swims are competitive they are available for anyone who can confidently swim the distance in the open ocean water and in sometimes challenging conditions.
Bondi Beach Splash And Dash -
There are three events that you can enter in the Bondi Splash Series .

The first, and newest addition to the event, is the Bondi Splash 1000 . This is a 1km swim that is quite unique in its approach to ocean water swims. Rather than one straight swim of 1000 metres you swim out 250m, return 250m to shore and repeat. This is great for first time ocean water swimmers who have done the training but may be a little nervous about embarking on their first open water swim.

The second event on the day is the most popular event and combines running and swimming. Participants sprint 1km along the length of Bondi Beach, swim 1km back along the beach in open water to the race start line, before embarking on the initial 1km run again. The short distances, relative to other swim and run events, make this a fast-paced breath-taking sprint event. It is a lot of fun and a great challenge.

The Duck Dash is the final event on the day and to say it is different is an understatement. Entrants must run an inflatable duck 400m along the shore, then swim 300m whilst keeping hold of the duck. This is all done wearing flippers (including the run!).
Bondi To Bronte -

Bondi's most famous ocean swim race. This take entrants from the shores of Bondi Beach around the cliffs to Bronte Beach. This 2.4km race (distance varies based on the tide) is a long, challenging swim that is sometimes battered with heavy swell and strong currents. If you are a strong swimmer, though, this is an event you cannot afford to miss. The perspective of Bondi that you get swimming around the cliffs is pretty incredible.
Bondi Bluewater Challenge -

The Bondi Bluewater Challenge offers a 2.1km or 1km swim within the bay at Bondi Beach. There is also a 4km run that non-swimmers may be interested in. This race is straightforward and the number of entrants is lower than some others meaning it is a little less frantic at the start of the race. We highly recommend this swim if the weather forecast is favourable.
North Bondi Classic -

The North Bondi Classic swim is run by the lifeguards at North Bondi Surf Life Saving Club and has a 1km or 2km race distance. The races start in front of the North Bondi Surf Life Saving Club and is contained with the bay of Bondi Beach. This event is popular with hundreds of entrants and there is always a great atmosphere on the day.
North Bondi Roughwater Classic -
The second race held by the North Bondi Surf Life Saving Club this race follows the same format as the North Bondi Classic swim. Another great day out for ocean water swimmers down at Bondi Beach.
South Head Roughwater -

So you think you can swim? The South Head Roughwater is a 10km open water swim from Bondi Beach to Watson's Bay. It commences at the end of summer as the colder weather begins to bite and conditions can get pretty tricky out there. If you're a very strong swimmer this is a great challenge to take. Did we mention there's a great pub - the Watson's Bay Hotel - at the finish line.

blocks.text: You've seen the mid-summer pictures of Bondi Beach filled with sunbathers under the blazing blue sky.
With more than 25,000 beaches in Australia why is Bondi the most famous of them all?

There are a few reasons why this eclectic beachside suburb attracts thousands of visitors every day. From its world-class restaurants, proximity to the Sydney CBD, relatively safe swimming conditions, and 1km strip of white sandy beach Bondi has rightly earned its reputation as one of Australia's top beaches.
Bondi Beach Restaurants

The restaurants in Bondi are second to none. From relaxed beach side spots such as Bucket List to the spectacularly situated celebrity haunt Bondi Icebergs there are restaurants to suit every taste. Visit our Eat section to learn more.
Bondi Beach Surfing and Swimming

Bondi's kilometre stretch of sand and great surf combine to make this one of the most enjoyable beaches to visit in summer. Patrolled by the Bondi Lifeguards it is vital that you swim between the flags to ensure you are being watched at all times. And if you are not a strong swimmer do not wade into the water beyond waist height. Whilst Bondi is safer than most beaches it can still be very dangerous for those unfamiliar with ocean swimming. Visit our swimming guide for more information about swimming at Bondi.
Getting from the city to Bondi Beach

Bondi Beach is the simplest beach to get to from the Sydney city CBD. You can catch a bus directly from the CBD or, if it's a busy weekend with lots of traffic, it is quicker to catch a train to Bondi Junction before catching a short bus trip to the beach. See our transport guide for more.

title: Bondi Icebergs - The famous Bondi pool - Visit Bondi Beach
metaDescription: Bondi Icebergs, the ocean pool at the southern end of Bondi Beach - what makes it the most photographed pool in the world, and how to visit it.
h1: Bondi Icebergs - The famous Bondi pool
intro: Bondi Icebergs - The famous Bondi pool — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Icebergs - The famous Bondi pool It is the most photographed pool in the world, recognisable all over the world. Bondi Icebergs is perched at the southern end of Bondi Beach, jutting out from the cliff sitting in the middle of th

blocks.text: It is the most photographed pool in the world, recognisable all over the world. Bondi Icebergs is perched at the southern end of Bondi Beach, jutting out from the cliff sitting in the middle of the ocean.

The most commonly asked question by those visiting Bondi is; can the public swim at Bondi Icebergs pool? The good news is that they can and it only costs $6.50 for adults, $4.50 for children, and $4.50 for spectators accompanying friends or family.

The pool was established more than 100 years ago and features both a 50m lap pool and a shallow kids pool adjacent to it. To become an official 'Bondi Iceberg' member swimmers must complete swims 3 out of 4 Sundays each month in winter over 5 years. If a swimming member fails to swim on at least 3 Sundays they must provide a written letter of explanation before the end of the relevant month.

The pool is open from 6am to 6.30pm every day except for Thursday when it is emptied, cleaned and refilled. In summer, the pool will often open on Thursday afternoon if the clean is completed in quick time but there is no guarantee of this.

The lanes at Bondi Icebergs pool are actually double the size of a normal lane meaning you follow on black line, on the left hand side, and return on the other line, again on the left hand side as you are swimming.

For more serious ocean swimmers you can access the ocean from Bondi Icebergs through a small gate at the end of the pool. Some people do the 'point to point' swim which is a lap of the beach and back again which is exactly 2km.
If swimming in the cooler months, the sauna provides a great spot to warm up pre and/or post-swim and is included in the price of admission.
For more information about where else you can swim at Bondi, click here .

title: Call On Dee - Visit Bondi Beach
metaDescription: What is Deanne Barry, from the famous Call On Me music clip up to now? Find out here.
intro: Call On Dee — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach Call On Dee Remember the Call On Me music video? blocks.text: Remember the Call On Me music video? You know, the one featuring several women and a man performing aerobics in a sexually suggestive manner to the now famous Eric Prydz track. At the time it was the most risqué mainstream music video ever released.
Of course you remember it.

What you probably don’t know is that the lead in that music video, Deanne Berry, who played the aerobics instructor runs a dance and fitness class right in the heart of Bondi with classes that have as much energy and creative choreography as the film clip itself.
Everyone we know who goes to the class loves it. And they probably won’t be happy that we are letting the secret out that this is the most fun fitness class you will likely find in the area.
We asked Deanne a few questions about her DJ Bodies class and about that music video.
Tell us a little bit about your dance and fitness class.

djBodies is a Dance conditioning class myself and business partner Jessica Powell Antonini, have personally created. Using all the knowledge we have obtained working in both the dance and Fitness industries. In a djBodies class we share with you a taste of what it feels like to dance and perform to your favourite artists!

Each workout is themed to a different Pop Artist, so you will dance your way through the sexy sounds of Rhianna, Kylie, Ariana Grande, Selena Gomez, Janet and Michael Jackson, JT, Madonna, Beyonce, Kanye, Usher and many more of your fave artists.

When you step into a djBodies class you will work on increasing stamina, flexibility and strength, while letting loose and leaving all your inhibitions at the door, feeling like your favourite Pop star!
Do you ever get recognised for starring in the Call On Me music video?

Being back in Oz, the general public are much more laid back! I don’t get recognised the way I did while being over in the UK but I guess now running around with two little ones you wouldn’t pick me as the sexy instructor wearing that naughty black thong leotard! Ha!
Do any of the dance moves in the film clip feature in your class?

I quite often get requests to re-create the “Call on me moves” both in djBodies classes and for live PA’s at parties or events and I still get SO much enjoyment out of dancing / teaching and performing the sexy track! So if you happen to be planning an 80's inspired event you might like to book dj Bodies to add some “call on me” fun!
How did you land the part in the music video?

My career started at the age of 16 living and working as a dancer / performer based in Sydney, but travelling to other states and Asia for various jobs touring with musicals and artists. Dancing for artists such as Kylie and Dani Minogue, Kanye West, Shaggy, Girls Aloud, Basement Jaxx, Neyo, Take that to name a few, I then landed a tour back up dancing for the iconic Sir Cliff Richard throughout Oz and NZ and he then offered for me to join his UK tour. After performing for a few weeks at the Royal Albert hall I had a break between concert dates so decided to join a few agencies to see if I could pick up any extra gigs. That was when I went for my first casting in London and it happened to be for a part in the 80’s inspired Ministry of Sound “Call On Me” video by Eric Prydz. I landed the job of the instructor and found myself a few days later dressed in that high cut black thong leotard, legwarms, sweatbands and not much else!
Did you have any inkling that the music video would become one of the most famous of all time?

I thought not too many people would see it so it would be fine to pelvic thrust and jump around a bit. Then the song and video became a huge hit, and it was the first time a club track had made the pop charts at number one and stayed there for 8 weeks! The video ended up in countries all over the world! And my face and butt was planted on the front of CD covers everywhere! It was pretty crazy! But I went from being a dancer, to all of a sudden being some Fitness Guru! Offers were flying in so I acted fast, took base in London, enrolled in some fitness courses and using my training knowledge as a dancer I had used my whole life, I entered the fitness industry.

My next offer was to choreograph and present Ministry of Sounds first ever Fitness DVD “Pump it up” which became one of the highest selling fitness DVD’s. I continued to make more DVD's for Ministry and also Universal Pictures.
I also took on the role as a Fitness presenter for GMTV (Britain’s Good morning TV) where I would wake up the country with various workouts. It was pretty crazy!
For first timers to your class what advice do you have for them?

My advice for first timers in a djBodies class, is to leave all your inhibitions at the door. Come in with an open mind, get ready to sweat, work hard and have loads of fun! And don’t worry, you don’t need to be a dancer to join in! I have mums and daughters doing our classes together! You don’t need any dance experience… just a love of moving to music!
How do people book and where can they find more information?
You can book in online www.deanneberrybodies.com The website also has some more info and contact details for any queries you might have!
When you are not in your studio where do you like to eat and drink in Bondi?

When I'm not in the studio (MPower Pilates) working out... my fave hangout in Bondi is just down the road from the studio on Curlewis st, at The Shop & Wine Bar, the perfect place to grab a coffee and brekky after class!
Another fave of mine is BRU coffee in North Bondi... only small but coffee is great!

title: Where to Swim at Bondi Beach
metaDescription: The best places to swim at Bondi Beach - between the flags, the Icebergs ocean pool and the North Bondi kids' pool. A local guide to swimming safely.
h1: Where to swim at Bondi Beach
intro: Swimming at Bondi Beach — Visit Bondi Beach Visit Bondi Beach Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Bondi Beach Guide What's On Swim Accommodation Tours Bondi Icebergs Gallery About Visit Bondi Beach SWIMMING AT BONDI BEACH A trip to Bondi Beach wouldn't be complete without taking a dip in its inviting waters. blocks.text: A trip to Bondi Beach wouldn't be complete without taking a dip in its inviting waters. There are three swimming options for visitors: the beach itself, Bondi's ocean pools, and indoor swimming facilities.
Here, we provide an overview of these choices and our recommendations.
Bondi Icebergs Ocean Pool

One of the most frequently asked questions by visitors to Bondi Beach is whether the public can swim at the iconic Bondi Icebergs pool. Fortunately, the answer is yes! The entry fee is a reasonable $9 for adults and $6 for children, offering an unforgettable swimming experience at this historic location.

Established over a century ago, Bondi Icebergs boasts a 50-meter lap pool along with a shallow kids' pool adjacent to it, providing swimming options for both adults and children. A lifeguard is always present to ensure the safety and well-being of all swimmers.

Bondi Icebergs pool is open daily from 6am weekdays and 6.30am on weekends and closes at 6:30 pm, except on Thursdays when it is closed to be drained, cleaned, and refilled. During the summer months, if the cleaning process is completed quickly, the pool may reopen on Thursday afternoons, but this is not guaranteed.

Interestingly, the lanes at Bondi Icebergs pool are double the width of standard swimming lanes. This unique design means swimmers follow the black line on the left-hand side and return on the other line, again on the left-hand side, providing ample space for swimmers of all levels.

For more experienced ocean swimmers, the pool offers direct access to the ocean through a small gate at its end. Many swimmers enjoy the "point to point" swim, which entails a lap across the beach and back, totalling exactly 2 kilometres.
During cooler months, the on-site sauna is the perfect spot to warm up before and/or after your swim and is included in the price of admission.

Bondi Icebergs also features a cafe, The Crabbe Hole, which serves delicious coffee and snacks on a decking area overlooking the pool, allowing you to relax and take in the stunning views after your swim.
Kids Ocean Pool, North Bondi

For families with young children or those who prefer a more low-key swimming experience, North Bondi’s Wally Weekes Ocean Pool is an ideal alternative. This simple rock pool offers a safe and enjoyable space for youngsters and less confident swimmers to cool down and have fun without venturing into the surf. The rock pools behind the small ocean pool itself is great for spotting crabs in the rock wall but be warned, when the waves are up the rock pool can become a wave pool unsuitable for kids.
Beach Swimming

Bondi Beach is one of Australia's most famous beaches, and for good reason. With its golden sands, crystal-clear waters, and fantastic surf, there's no better place to take a refreshing dip. While Bondi Icebergs is a popular swimming spot, it’s off the sand directly from the beach itself where the majority of swimmers at Bondi will be found. Dive in and explore the different swimming experiences Bondi Beach has to offer.

North Bondi The northern end of Bondi Beach is generally more sheltered and calmer than the rest of the beach, making it an ideal spot for families and those who prefer a more relaxed swim. The water here is shallower and typically has fewer waves, making it perfect for wading, floating, or swimming laps close to shore. The area is patrolled by lifeguards and is also home to the North Bondi Surf Life Saving Club.

South Bondi The southern end of Bondi Beach is more popular among experienced swimmers and surfers due to its stronger currents and larger waves. While the conditions here can be more challenging, it's an exciting spot for confident swimmers seeking a thrilling experience. Always be cautious and swim between the red and yellow flags, as this area is patrolled by lifeguards.

Surf Swimming For adrenaline-seekers and experienced swimmers, catching waves at Bondi Beach can be an exhilarating experience. The middle section of the beach is popular for surf swimming, but always exercise caution and pay attention to the lifeguards' advice. If you're new to surf swimming, don’t assume you will be okay taking on Bondi’s surf. It can be treacherous and drownings can occur. Always play it safe!

Rock Pools and Tidal Pools If you're up for a little exploration, Bondi Beach has several rock pools and tidal pools to discover. These natural formations can be found along the shoreline and are perfect for a more secluded and tranquil swim. Be cautious of slippery rocks and changing tides, and always swim with a buddy.

No matter your swimming preferences, Bondi Beach has a spot for everyone. From calm, sheltered waters to exhilarating surf breaks, there's a swimming experience here for every skill level and adventure-seeker. Remember to always swim between the red and yellow flags, follow lifeguard instructions, and be aware of your surroundings to ensure a safe and enjoyable time in the water.
These videos provide some helpful information for novice beach swimmers but all you really need to know is swim between the flags - we can’t say this enough.
Indoor Swimming

For swimmers who are looking for a more traditional swimming experience they can access the Speedo Fitness Club which has a 25m indoor heated swimming pool and is located on Campbell Parade. If you visit their website you can get a free 1 day trial.

The Local’s Guide to Sydney’s Bondi Beach Golden sand, legendary surf and a café scene that could make anyone late for a meeting. Welcome to Bondi - Sydney’s most famous beach and the perfect place for sunrise runs, coastal walks, family day

blocks.text: Golden sand, legendary surf and a café scene that could make anyone late for a meeting. Welcome to Bondi - Sydney’s most famous beach and the perfect place for sunrise runs, coastal walks, family days and laid-back long lunches. Use this local guide to plan a 3-hour, half-day or full-day Bondi adventure, find the best photo spots and discover the small, local places visitors miss.
Introduction

Bondi is more than a postcard - it’s a lived-in beach town with surf culture, community markets, a dramatic ocean pool and a coastal walk that serves up cliff views every few minutes. This guide gives clear routes, timing tips (when to arrive, when to avoid crowds), top cafés, safety notes and three ready-to-use itineraries so you can see Bondi like a local.
Top Things to Do in Bondi
Bondi Beach - swim, sun and people-watch

Bondi’s crescent of golden sand is where lifeguards, locals and travelers meet. The northern end is where you’ll often find the surfboard crowd and surf lessons; the middle is busy with sunbathers and volleyball; the southern end tapers toward the Icebergs precinct and the start of the coastal walk. Mornings (sunrise-9am) are perfect for a peaceful swim, a sunrise run and coffee; late afternoons are for long walks and softer light for photos. Lifeguard flags mark the safest swim zones - always swim between them.
Want to know where you should sit on the beach. Here’s our full guide.
Bondi Icebergs & the ocean pool - iconic photos & an ocean dip

Perched at Bondi’s southern edge, Bondi Icebergs is an instantly recognisable ocean pool that frames raw surf and dramatic winter waves. Beyond the photo op, Icebergs is a place to swim in sea-splashed saltwater in a safe, managed pool with café facilities and a small museum area about its winter swimming club. Come mid-morning for coffee and people-watching, or time a dip at high tide to feel the ocean’s energy - the contrast of calm pool water against the crashing waves is unforgettable.
We’ve created the most comprehensive guide to Bondi Icebergs here.
Bondi To Coogee coastal walk - 6 km of cliff views

The Bondi to Coogee walk is a roughly 6 km coastal route linking Bondi, Tamarama, Bronte and Coogee with constant ocean panoramas, rocky headlands and secluded beaches tucked in between. Walk at a relaxed pace (2-3 hours) and stop at the scenic lookouts, sculptural art, cafes and seaside parks. It’s ideal for photographers, active days, and families who want a predictable route with toilets, cafés and occasional shady spots. Wear good shoes, bring water and take sunscreen - there are short stair sections and exposed cliffs.
We’ve created a full guide to the walk here.
Bondi Pavilion & Markets - culture, craft and weekend buzz

The Bondi Pavilion sits above the sand as Bondi’s cultural hub: community theatre, workshops, art shows and a calendar of events. Weekends often bring stalls and a small market atmosphere - local makers, vintage finds and street food. The Pavilion is also a good place to pick up local maps, sign up for classes (yoga/sea-swim briefings) and find event listings for the time you’re visiting. It’s where the community calendar and visitor culture meet - check the Pavilion noticeboard or the events page before you go.
See our Bondi Market guide here.
Cafe & brunch crawl - where locals queue for coffee

Bondi’s café scene blends specialty coffee, creative brunches and no-frills bakeries. Early morning espresso spots near the park cater to runners; mid-morning brunch places fill up fast, especially on weekends. Walk down Bondi Road and the lanes off Campbell Parade for hidden favourites - think crisp sourdough, seasonal smashed avo and great takeaway pastries if you’re short on time. Tip: aim for a coffee before 9am to avoid queues, or book a late brunch reservation if you’re visiting on a weekend.
Need some tips? Here are our top 10 Bondi cafes in 2025.
Surf lessons & gear hire - catch your first wave

Bondi is a top place to take a surf lesson thanks to consistent beginner waves and professional instructors operating from the sand. Lessons typically include basic theory, a short beach briefing and guided time with foam boards in the white water. There are multiple surf schools and rental stands where you can hire boards and wetsuits by the hour. If you’re nervous, choose a small group lesson or a private session and check the daily surf and flag conditions with the lifeguards - they’ll advise on safe zones and the best time to learn. You can see our full Bondi Surf guide here.
Three ready-to-use itineraries
3-hour Bondi (perfect for tight schedules)
Sunrise stretch or 30-minute run along the beach promenade.
Coffee and a quick croissant at a local espresso bar (arrive before 9am).
Short walk to the Icebergs viewpoint for photos and a swim, then stroll back along the sand. Great when you’re staying nearby or need a morning reset.
Half-day (3-5 hours)
Start with a relaxed swim or surf lesson.
Brunch at a local café (book ahead on weekends).
Walk the first section of the Bondi to Tamarama coastline, stop for an ice-cream and return via the Pavilion. Perfect for families or visitors who want a relaxed local feel.
Full-day (6+ hours)
Sunrise run or swim, breakfast at a top café.
Complete the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk with scenic stops at Tamarama and Bronte. Lunch at Coogee Pavillion.
Return to Bondi for sunset by the Icebergs pool. Ideal for photographers, walkers and those who love a full seaside day.
How to get to Bondi
From Sydney CBD: Regular buses run from the city and take ~20-30 minutes depending on traffic. Taxis and rideshares are convenient but can be slower in peak hours.

From Sydney Airport: A common route is train to the city then a direct bus or rideshare; time varies with traffic. Here’s a detailed guide to transport options from the airport including private transport, Uber, taxi, and train tips. Please Note: There has recently been an uptick in taxi scams from the airport and we currently recommend you avoid this option.
By foot/bike: Bondi is bike-friendly with hire options and pleasant promenades for a scenic approach.
Where to stay
Budget: Hostels and small guesthouses near Bondi Junction or Bondi Road. Great for short stays and easy transport links.
Mid: Boutique B&Bs and apartments a short walk from the sand - the sweet spot for comfort and location.
Premium: Ocean-view suites and beach hotels on Campbell Parade for uninterrupted sea views and sunset access.
Our tips for the best spots to stay can be found here.
Practical tips & safety
Swim between the flags: Lifeguards mark the safe swimming areas; surf conditions change daily. For more information see our full guide.
Sun sense: Use SPF, wear a hat and reapply often - the sun is strong year-round.
Beat the crowds: Arrive early (6-9am) for peaceful sand and easier parking; evenings are quieter after mid-afternoon. Here’s our guide to catching the perfect sunrise.
Accessibility: The beachfront and Pavilion have accessible entry points; check individual venues for detailed accessibility info. Check out this guide to wheelchair access at Bondi Beach.
Families: Bring a small shade shelter and pack snacks - there are playgrounds and grassy picnic areas near the beach.
FAQs
When is the best time to visit Bondi? Early morning for runs and coffee or late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds. Midday in peak season gets busy fast.
How long is the Bondi to Coogee walk? About 6 km total. Allow 1.5-3 hours at a relaxed pace with stops for photos and coffee.

Can I swim at Bondi year-round? Yes - lifeguards operate seasonally on a schedule. Check the flags and local notices; for open-water swimming the Icebergs pool is an iconic, safer alternative for choppier days. If you’re new to Bondi this swimming safety guide is essential.
Are dogs allowed on the beach? There are dog-friendly zones nearby but rules vary by season and location; check local signage before bringing a pet.
